jobs.title: Autonomy Test & Integration Engineer
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.



ROLE OVERVIEW

We're looking for an Autonomy Test & Integration Engineer to take our perception system from the bench to the open ocean and build the test infrastructure that connects the two. The system detects and tracks vessel traffic for a wing-in-ground-effect craft that takes off and lands on the water. Testing perception on this class of vehicle is a problem very few people have worked on.

Half the job happens on the water. You'll go out with our test and operations team, who run the vessels and the campaigns, and handle the perception side: mounting and cabling cameras and radar on boats, calibrating dockside, and collecting data against live vessel traffic. No two sea days give you the same weather, light, and traffic. The job is planning each one tightly, adapting when hardware or the sea won't cooperate, and coming back with data worth keeping.

The other half is onshore, building what the field work depends on: replay and hardware-in-the-loop setups that let us rerun a sea day on the bench, calibration tooling that keeps sensor data usable, and the integration path that carries new perception software onto our vehicles. Whether a day's results can be trusted comes down to calibration and process, and both are yours. The team iterates as fast as this infrastructure lets it.

Major perception test campaigns are on the calendar for the next year. They'll run on infrastructure and process this role builds between now and then.

If you’re energized by working at the intersection of cutting-edge innovation, real-world impact, and hands-on engineering, you’ll be in the right place - and we’d be thrilled to have you on the team!




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run perception field tests. Define what a test day must produce, set up and calibrate the perception sensor rigs, and run sensor tests on surrogate vessels with our test and operations team.

 - Do hands-on integration work. Bring software changes onto real vehicle hardware and troubleshoot what breaks in that transition, across every platform the team supports.

 - Own the replay tooling. Operate and extend the hardware-in-the-loop and data-replay infrastructure the team's testing runs on, building on existing recording and evaluation tooling.

 - Keep perception reliable. Track and maintain perception system reliability across every platform the team supports.

 - Test and sign off on software changes. Review changes and decide when they're ready to move from the bench, to hardware-in-the-loop replay, to a surrogate vessel, to a vehicle.

 - Carry capability to missions. Take the perception capabilities the team builds and apply them to customer and U.S. defense missions, working with our mission software team to define the mission-specific functions needed and bringing those needs back to the perception team.

 - Define autonomy test scenarios. As our autonomy work grows beyond alerting, design the scenarios that prove out new autonomy algorithms and run them with our test and operations team.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Demonstrated professional experience in robotics, autonomy, or perception software, including hands-on hardware-in-the-loop or data-replay work.

 - Field deployment experience, ideally including sensor testing on boats or a comparable surrogate vehicle.

 - Experience testing software on real hardware, from code review through deployment.

 - Strong C/C++ for real-time or embedded systems, working Python, and comfort administering Linux systems.

 - Eligibility: this position is subject to U.S. export control regulations; applicants must be U.S. persons as defined by ITAR (22 CFR 120.62).

 - Bonus: familiarity with autonomy algorithm concepts, ARPA radar tracking experience, boating or sea-trials background, ground-truth system experience, basic electrical troubleshooting, DO-178C familiarity.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You know field testing is a team effort. You work closely with perception, autonomy, test, operations, and mission software teams to plan effectively, solve problems in real time, and make sure what you learn on the water gets back to the people building the system. You communicate clearly, especially when conditions change or something isn't ready to move forward.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You’re hands-on and like getting to the bottom of why something isn’t working. Whether it’s a sensor, calibration issue, software integration problem, or test setup, you dig in yourself, troubleshoot across hardware and software, and look for ways to make the underlying tooling or process better — not just get through the test day.

 - Adaptable & Agile: You’re comfortable on a boat, not just at a desk. You know field testing rarely goes exactly as planned and can adapt when weather, hardware, vessel traffic, or test conditions change. You stay focused on what the test needs to prove and make good calls about when to adjust, keep going, or stop and regroup.

 - Innovative Mindset: You see the whole path from the bench to hardware-in-the-loop testing to a surrogate vessel and ultimately the vehicle, and you’re always looking for ways to make that path faster, more reliable, and more repeatable. You hold a high bar for testing and validation and don’t sign off on something simply because the team is in a hurry — you want the data and evidence to know it’s ready.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation including a robust equity incentive plan.

 - Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance - we cover 100% of your premiums.

 - 401(k) with company matching, so you can plan for the future.

 - Generous flexible time off, paid parental leave, and company-wide holiday breaks.

 - Relocation packages available for those moving to join our team.

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

Equal Opportunity Employer

REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Machine Operator - 2nd Shift
jobs.description:
Machine Operator I is an entry-level machine operator position responsible for safely operating and monitoring assigned production equipment. Under the guidance of experienced operators and supervisors, the incumbent performs basic machine adjustments, quality checks, sanitation activities, and routine equipment operation tasks while developing proficiency on assigned equipment. This role supports the production of high-quality products by adhering to safety, food safety, quality, and operational standards.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Safety and Compliance

• Follow all company safety policies, GMPs, food safety requirements, and quality standards.
• Wear required PPE and comply with all safety procedures.
• Follow Lockout/Tagout procedures when performing equipment cleaning, maintenance support, or troubleshooting activities.
• Handle cleaning chemicals safely and according to established procedures.
• Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.

Equipment Operation

• Set up, start up, operate, monitor, and shut down production equipment according to established standards.
• Perform machine adjustments based on product specifications, packaging requirements, and operating conditions.
• Monitor machine performance and product flow throughout production runs.
• Detect and respond to machine malfunctions, equipment abnormalities, and product defects.
• Stop, reset, and restart equipment safely following established procedures.
• Clear jams and minor equipment issues while minimizing downtime.
• Perform product changeovers efficiently while maintaining quality and food safety standards.

Quality Assurance

• Perform required quality checks, inspections, and product evaluations.
• Verify fill weights, package integrity, coding accuracy, and product appearance.
• Identify, communicate, and assist in resolving quality concerns.
• Complete all required quality documentation accurately and on time.
• Ensure products consistently meet customer and company specifications.

Sanitation and Cleaning

• Perform equipment teardown, cleaning, sanitization, and reassembly activities.
• Clean pumps, sanitary piping, fillers, conveyors, and associated production equipment.
• Operate CIP systems as required.
• Verify equipment cleanliness and readiness prior to production startup.
• Report any sanitation or quality concerns immediately.

Equipment Care and Maintenance

• Perform routine inspections of equipment and identify potential mechanical issues.
• Complete assigned autonomous maintenance activities and MSS tasks.
• Assist maintenance personnel with preventative maintenance and repair activities as needed.
• Communicate equipment performance concerns to supervisors and maintenance teams.
• Help reduce downtime through proactive equipment monitoring and troubleshooting.

Production Documentation

• Accurately complete all production records, downtime reports, quality checks, sanitation records, and operational documentation.
• Record downtime events and root causes within company systems.
• Maintain accurate production and efficiency data.

Continuous Improvement

• Identify opportunities to improve safety, quality, efficiency, waste reduction, and equipment performance.
• Participate in continuous improvement initiatives and problem-solving activities.
• Support departmental goals related to OEE, productivity, quality, and cost control.

Education: High school diploma or GED required.

Related Experience: Previous relevant experience, preferably in a manufacturing environment.

Equipment/Software Skills: Ability to operate production equipment safely and effectively. Basic mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills. Ability to read and follow work instructions, SOPs, and production schedules.

Competencies

• Employees are encouraged to participate in efficiency and safety improvement teams
• Strong communication and teamwork skills.
• Learn and follow written rules and procedures
• Produce accurate documentation
• Maintain acceptable attendance
• Will have the opportunity to learn various positions
• Must fill in when needed in temporary/permanent vacancies

Physical: Must be able to walk throughout the plant, to include walking and climbing up/downstairs and ladders (portable, fixed).  Must have be ability to lift up to 50 pounds occasionally is required.

Sensory: Must have the appropriate level of sensory acuity (visual, hearing, speaking, smell and touch) to be able to identify and react to normal, abnormal and alarm conditions (chemicals, temperature, etc.)

Mental/Reasoning: Must be able to logically and methodically work through and break down complex problems and processes to enable effective communication with all levels of the organization

Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision

jobs.title: Account Executive
jobs.description:
Stuut is transforming how B2B companies turn revenue into cash. Businesses worldwide have trillions tied up in receivables, yet the work between order and payment still relies on fragmented systems and labor-intensive manual processes. Stuut’s AI agent works across order management, credit, collections, payments, cash application, disputes and deductions, carrying context through every step. Customers reduce DSO by 47%, collect 40% more cash and eliminate 70% of manual work without replacing their ERP.

Stuut is already trusted by finance teams at companies including Honeywell, Medtronic and ZoomInfo, from Fortune 10 enterprises to scaling mid-market businesses. We are backed by a16z, Khosla Ventures, Activant, 1984 Ventures, Page One and Microsoft.



The Role
We’re hiring an Account Executive to own the full sales cycle, build relationships with customers, and drive new revenue for Stuut. You’ll work closely with marketing, BDRs, and our founders to turn curiosity into committed customers. From high-volume prospecting to contract negotiation, you’ll craft tailored sales motions that connect our AI-powered financial workflow platform to the real challenges facing manufacturing, distribution, and other core industries.



You’ll set the bar for modern sales at Stuut—balancing persistence with precision and consultative insight with a bias for action.



What You’ll Do

 - Own the full sales cycle from prospecting to close, including discovery, demos, and contract negotiation.

 - Build and maintain a healthy pipeline in HubSpot with accurate forecasting and reporting.

 - Create omnichannel outreach strategies (phone, email, LinkedIn) to engage decision-makers and drive meetings.

 - Collaborate with marketing and BDR teams to qualify leads and convert them into high-value customers.

 - Develop account plans to expand adoption and revenue within existing mid-market customers.

 - Represent Stuut at industry events, webinars, and networking opportunities.

 - Share customer insights with Product and Marketing to shape features, messaging, and go-to-market strategies.



You Might Be a Fit If You…

 - You have an ownership mentality and are excited to take on responsibility

 - Have 4+ years of experience selling B2B SaaS.

 - Are equally comfortable picking up the phone 100+ times a day and delivering high-impact demos.

 - Know how to build trust quickly and tailor solutions to specific business challenges.

 - Use data and CRM discipline to manage your pipeline and improve conversion rates.

 - Thrive in a fast-moving startup environment and take ownership of your results.

 - Have experience working cross-functionally with marketing and product teams.

Compensation

 - Top-of-market salary and equity package

 - Benefits (for U.S.-based full-time employees)

 - Medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you

 - 401(k) & Match

 - Equity

 - Flexible PTO

 - Parental Leave

jobs.title: Demand Generation Manager, Lead Gen
jobs.description:
At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

This role will be based in San Francisco Bay Area or New York City.

We are looking for a performance-driven growth marketer to own the execution, optimization, and performance of scaled lead generation campaigns. This role is responsible for managing day-to-day campaign health across acquisition channels, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and conversion, and leveraging data-driven insights to design new campaigns that can deliver revenue impact.

As a Lead Generation Manager, you will translate quarterly targets into channel execution plans, manage weekly lead volume performance, and drive test iterations to improve conversion across targeting strategy and creative materials. You’ll partner closely with Product Marketing, Marketing Operations, and channel owners to leverage the right messaging, localization strategy, and ensure accurate tracking, targeting, and lead routing are in place for all new campaign launches. You will also partner closely with Sales and Sales Ops to ensure leads are qualified, prioritized, and converted effectively and analyze funnel performance to improve conversion rates and hit revenue targets.

This is an execution-focused role for someone who thrives in complex environments, managing multiple concurrent launches while maintaining strong attention to detail and delivering coordinated, cross-functional campaigns that drive measurable results.

Responsibilities:

• Own campaign execution and performance across scaled demand generation campaigns (e.g. email, LinkedIn), delivering against lead volume, SQOs, and revenue targets.
• Manage campaign performance end‑to‑end, analyzing engagement, lead volume, and conversion rates to identify drivers for success and opportunities to optimize strategy.
• Develop and execute campaign roadmaps across targeting, segmentation, personalization, messaging, and creative to improve campaign outcomes.
• Partner with channel owners and ops partners to monitor campaign health, troubleshoot issues, and ensure accurate tracking and lead routing.
• Analyze data insights and campaign learnings and translate into actionable recommendations that improve performance.
• Leverage and/or build AI tools to enhance operational efficiency and drive measurable, real lift in program and campaign performance.
• Communicate strategy and performance that inform decisions and influence stakeholders.

Basic Qualifications:

• BA/BS degree in marketing, business, or a related field.
• 5+ years of growth marketing experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Proven experience running scaled demand generation programs across channels (paid, email, web) with a focus on execution and performance optimization
• Creative marketer with a passion for understanding the audience and designing programs that inspire action.
• Exceptional interpersonal, communication (oral and written), and presentation skills.
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret funnel metrics, identify performance drivers, and translate insights into actionable optimizations.
• Ability to prioritize, balance multiple projects, and manage complex workstreams while consistently delivering results.
• Experience collaborating across time zones to develop global strategies.
• Strong ability to collaborate, build deep relationships with colleagues, and influence functional teams to achieve goals.
• Experience working with Sales teams. Direct Sales experience or prior roles working closely with Sales leadership is a plus.

Suggested Skills:

• Cross-functional Collaboration
• Strong Business Acumen
• Stakeholder Management

jobs.title: Golf Shop Guest Service Attendant
jobs.description:
The base salary for this position is $19.00 hourly.

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager, Software
jobs.description:
About the role

We are seeking a Technical Project Manager (TPM) to drive cross-functional planning and execution for our Software programs. In this role, you will work closely with engineering leaders across software, hardware, science, and product to coordinate efforts from early concept through delivery to (literal!) launch. You will develop schedules and milestones, uncover gaps, flag risks, support resource planning, and ensure clear communication across stakeholders.

As a Software TPM, you’ll help teams stay aligned, unblock issues quickly, and deliver critical software capabilities that power Muon’s mission. You will provide the structure and process discipline required to scale our development efforts, while enabling teams to make fast, high-quality decisions in a complex, interdisciplinary environment.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

Responsibilities

• Program Planning & Roadmapping: Define objectives, scope, milestones, and success criteria in collaboration with engineering and product stakeholders.

• Scheduling & Execution Management: Build and maintain project timelines, track dependencies, monitor progress, and adjust plans as priorities shift.

• Risk & Issue Management: Identify risks early, coordinate mitigation plans, surface blockers, and drive timely resolution.

• Cross-Functional Coordination: Facilitate collaboration across software, hardware, science, and product teams, ensuring aligned deliverables and clear handoffs.

• Communication & Reporting: Provide concise, actionable updates to stakeholders and leadership on progress, changes, risks, and decisions.

• Process & Continuous Improvement: Identify inefficiencies in workflows, propose improvements, and help implement better practices and tools.

• Resource & Capacity Planning: Assist in forecasting resource needs, tracking capacity, and supporting prioritization and staffing decisions.

• Release Planning & Readiness: Coordinate software releases, track readiness criteria, and communicate expectations to impacted teams.

Qualifications

• BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

• Demonstrated ability to establish and optimize software project management processes.

• Strong technical background with knowledge of software development methods, tools, and infrastructure.

• Proven ability to communicate effectively with diverse technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Experience leading cross-functional planning, scheduling, and risk management across multiple teams.

• Results-oriented mindset with a bias toward clarity, accountability, and continuous improvement.

• Excited to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with evolving priorities.

Nice to have

• Experience in aerospace, robotics, logistics, or other domains with real-time high-reliability software development requirements.

• Experience reviewing technical documentation, architecture proposals, or requirements specifications.

• Comfort with Jira, Confluence and other productivity tools

• Exposure to OKR or goal-setting frameworks, and alignment of program priorities with company objectives.

• Ability to work effectively in distributed team environments.

Salary

The salary range for this role is $158,000 - $180,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too.  Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

jobs.title: Product Leader, Prefill
jobs.description:
SentiLink https://www.sentilink.com/ provides innovative identity and risk solutions, empowering institutions and individuals to transact with confidence. We’re building the future of identity verification in the United States replacing a clunky, ineffective, and expensive status quo with solutions that are 10x faster, smarter, and more accurate.

Our real-time APIs have helped verify hundreds of millions of identities, starting with financial services and rapidly expanding into new markets. SentiLink supports a variety of ways to work, ranging from fully remote to in-office. We operate as a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India. We maintain physical offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India. If you’re located near one of these offices, we would love for you to spend time in the office regularly. Some roles are hybrid or in-office by design. For example, our engineering team in India works primarily from our Gurugram office.

 


ROLE:

We’re looking for a leader with a technical background and deep understanding of data to build SentiLink’s identity resolution suite, including prefill, identity completion, and pinning. As part of this scope you will also be responsible for our underlying data merging and keying and linking technology and processes.

In this role, you will partner with teams across the company to understand how internal systems and datasets are used today and what they must support as we scale. You will translate varied internal needs into clear product requirements, prioritize improvements, and drive delivery from concept through adoption.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own the product vision, roadmap, and execution for internal technical initiatives, with a strong focus on data‐intensive systems and foundational datasets.

 - Lead cross-functional efforts to improve the quality, reliability, and usability of internal systems, including datasets, shared services, and internal platforms.

 - Drive long-term initiatives to future-proof internal data and technology assets, ensuring they scale with evolving product, analytics, and operational needs.

 - Partner with engineering, data science, solutions analytics, and product stakeholders to understand use cases, clarify requirements, and identify interdependencies.

 - Manage prioritization across competing internal demands, balancing immediate impact with long-term strategic value.

 - Translate complex internal needs into clear, actionable specifications and ensure alignment across teams.

 - Apply structured project management to initiatives with multiple teams, ambiguous problem spaces, and intricate technical dependencies.

 - Define and track success metrics for internal systems and datasets, such as quality, completeness, latency, reliability, and stakeholder satisfaction.

 - Communicate roadmap, progress, risks, and tradeoffs to internal stakeholders at all levels.

 


REQUIREMENTS:

 - 5+ years of experience with data-heavy or platform-oriented products, with a focus on data platform.

 - Hands-on experience working with large datasets, ideally in distributed or big-data environments (e.g., Spark, Databricks, BigQuery, Snowflake, similar).

 - Strong understanding of big data concepts, data pipelines, data cleaning/normalization, and data modeling.

 - Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with engineering, data science, and analytics teams on deeply technical problem spaces.

 - Experience driving large internal initiatives with multiple stakeholders and managing substantial cross-functional dependencies.

 - Proven ability to structure ambiguous requirements, prioritize effectively, and deliver predictable execution on complex technical programs.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences and facilitate alignment across teams.

 - A forward-looking, durability-focused mindset—ensuring internal systems and datasets are built for scale, maintainability, and long-term adaptability.

 


SALARY RANGE:

 - Home office stipend, and more!

jobs.title: Staff Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description:
WHAT TO EXPECT 

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron Power’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.




JOB OVERVIEW

As a Staff Supply Chain Manager, you’ll lead strategic sourcing for the critical components and assemblies that power Heron Link.  In this pivotal role, you’ll partner closely with the Head of Supply Chain and leaders across Finance, Design Engineering, NPI and Manufacturing to build a resilient supply base. You will ensure the commercial success of Heron’s supply chain, overseeing product cost and supplier performance. 




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Define and own the category strategies for key components and assemblies.

 - Achieve or exceed cost targets through data-driven should-cost modeling, market and commodity analysis, and disciplined negotiations.

 - Lead RFx processes and negotiate commercial agreements, including piece pricing, tooling/NRE, and key contractual terms.

 - Manage business risk through scenario assessment of capacity, geopolitics, logistics, and supplier technology / commercial roadmaps. Actively partner with the engineering team to identify/mitigate supply and demand challenges

 - Drive supplier readiness across prototype, pilot, and mass production builds to ensure smooth scale-up and launch execution.

 - Develop and execute the logistics and warehousing strategy associated with and in partnership with factory operations

 - Escalate key supply, cost, and/or quality issues with partner teams and collaboratively develop corrective action plans 




WHAT YOU WILL BRING

We’re open to early to mid-career candidates with or without leadership experience. Scope and responsibilities will scale with the right candidate.




MUST HAVE REQUIREMENTS 

 - 8+ years of experience in sourcing or procurement for high volume manufacturing

 - Degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business Administration, or equivalent experience

 - Deep category knowledge across mechanical, electrical (PCB/PCBA), and/or electro-mechanical components and assemblies

 - Strong negotiation and contract management skills

 - Experience leading cross-functional work-streams with engineering, operations, finance, legal and NPI teams to drive alignment and execute sourcing strategies

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

 - Willingness to travel domestically and internationally often with short notice




NICE TO HAVES

 - Extensive supply chain or manufacturing operations experience with power semiconductors, electronic components, injection molding, stamping, sheet metal fabrication, printed circuit board fab and assembly and adhesives 

 - Prior supplier development supporting medium voltage (34.5kV) or grid-related power electronics, such as converters, switchgear, circuit breakers, dielectric materials, and bussing

 - Strong data analysis and visualization skills (Tableau, PowerBI etc.) 
   
   

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power. 

Heron Power provides competitive compensation (salary and equity) and benefits.  The base salary range for the role is from $145,000 to $199,000.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Structures
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

As the Senior Manager, Structures, you’ll lead the team responsible for one of the most fundamental aspects of a safe, certifiable vehicle - ensuring our Seaglider can withstand everything it encounters in service, and proving it to the standards required for certification.

You’ll join an existing team of capable engineers and become their functional home: setting technical standards, developing careers, and building a cohesive, disciplined group that programs across REGENT can rely on. You’ll own the quality and consistency of structural analysis, margin documentation, and certification artifacts - not just for one program, but as a function.

Working closely with Loads & Dynamics, Flight Physics, and Manufacturing, you’ll own the structural side of critical cross-functional interfaces: how loads are applied, how margins are calculated, how FEM fidelity is maintained, and how test correlation closes the loop between analysis and reality.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Lead global finance operations. Accounting and reporting, month end close, financial controls, regulatory reporting, local audit, and regulatory reporting all sit under you. You'll lead a team of 30+ professionals across 15 countries and be accountable for the quality, timeliness, and defensibility of everything that comes out of it.

• Partner with the regional C-suite on what's next. Business strategy, exchange listings, infrastructure investment, and M&A — you'll be in the room, and you'll be the one putting numbers behind the options. Capital planning and investor relations sit with you, as do external partnerships that carry a financial dimension.

• Price the decisions before they're made. New products, new markets, new licenses. Each one gets a financial evaluation from your team — unit economics, capital requirements, tax and regulatory cost, downside cases. Leadership should be able to trust that analysis without re-running it.

• Tighten controls and risk frameworks across crypto and fiat. This is the part most finance leaders haven't done before. Internal controls, SOX readiness, audit, and global regulatory obligations have to work across digital-asset custody and movement as well as conventional banking flows. You'll build the frameworks that hold up in both worlds.

• Own external relationships. Regulators, banking partners, payment providers. These relationships determine what the business can and can't do in a given market, and they need a senior finance voice who regulators and bank credit committees take seriously.

jobs.title: Director, Clinical Quality & Compliance
jobs.description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

The Director, Clinical Quality & Compliance is responsible for the strategic oversight, management, and execution of clinical quality assurance and regulatory compliance programs across pre-market and post-market clinical research initiatives. The Director will work closely with internal Clinical Operations teams and cross-functional partners to support and monitor compliance, ensure adherence with FDA IDE requirements and Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and maintain inspection readiness across all studies, both  internally managed  and externally initiated or managed.

Job Responsibilities:

• Leads clinical quality and regulatory compliance strategies and initiatives across pre-market and post-market internal and external clinical programs.

• Ensures robust end-to-end clinical trial compliance with FDA Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines (21 CFR Parts 50, 56, 312, 812) and ISO 14155.

• Oversees medical device labeling requirements, ensuring full compliance with FDA regulations and international labeling standards for post-market and investigational devices.

• Authors, reviews, and maintains Investigator’s Brochures (IB) for investigational medical devices being used in clinical research programs.

• Leads Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO) audit preparation, internal GCP audits, vendor oversight, and external regulatory health authority inspections.

• Works closely with internal Clinical Operations and external CRO teams to ensure study protocols, execution strategies, and trial management practices align with regulatory and quality standards.

• Establishes clinical trial monitoring protocols and oversees key study deliverables, including Informed Consent Forms (ICFs), site monitoring oversight plans, and Trial Master File (TMF) quality standards.

• Partners with Clinical Operations to review regulatory document packages required for site greenlighting, ensuring ongoing Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Ethics Committee (EC) approvals, protocol amendments, and revised ICF implementations remain compliant across all sites.

• Manages regulatory compliance oversight for Unanticipated Adverse Device Effects (UADE) and Serious Adverse Event (SAE) reporting workflows, ensuring strict adherence to FDA 10-day reporting windows, IRB/EC notifications, and safety monitoring plans.

• Implements systematic oversight for logging, evaluating, and mitigating protocol deviations and non-compliance, ensuring thorough root-cause analysis (RCA) and Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) in partnership with internal Clinical Operations.

• Partners with Clinical Operations to establish quality oversight and compliance metrics ensuring field monitors and study personnel execute the trial strictly per the approved protocol and Instructions for Use (IFU).

• Partners with Regulatory Affairs to ensure post-market regulatory obligations are met, including contribution and review of Clinical Evaluation Reports (CER), Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) studies, Literature Searches, and Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSUR).

• Contributes to FDA Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) regulatory strategies and submissions.

• Navigates geographic data governance, data privacy, and cross-border clinical regulatory requirements for multi-site global trials.

• Participates in and leads process improvement activities within the department and cross-functionally alongside Clinical Operations.

• Perform other duties, as necessary.

Skills Needed:

• Deep technical knowledge of FDA IDE regulations, FDA GCP standards, ISO 14155, and medical device labeling requirements.

• Strong experience partnering closely with internal Clinical Operations teams to ensure robust GCP compliance in study management processes.

• Direct hands-on experience hosting FDA BIMO audits and preparing sponsors/vendors for regulatory health authority inspections.

• Demonstrated expertise reviewing and managing ICFs, IBs, IFUs, PMCF plans, and PSUR compilation.

• Extensive background managing protocol deviations, CAPA systems, and UADE/SAE safety reporting within regulated clinical trials.

• Understanding of multi-geographic clinical trial execution, data integrity, and cross-border regulatory considerations.

• Strong matrix leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to drive cross-functional compliance.

• Incredible attention to detail, accuracy, and quality.

• Ability to manage multiple tasks and work comfortably in an environment with shifting priorities.

• Ability to work in a collaborative team environment with a willing, all-hands-on-deck attitude.

• Excellent written and oral English communication skills required.

• Proficiency in computer programs, specifically Microsoft Office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and Google tools.

Educational Requirements & Work Experience:

• Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Biomedical Engineering, Clinical Research, or related scientific/health field (Master's, Ph.D., PharmD, or RN preferred).

• Demonstrated minimum of 8 years relevant experience in clinical quality assurance and regulatory affairs within the medical device, biotech, or combination product industries.

• Demonstrated experience leading BIMO audit readiness and FDA IDE submissions preferred.

• Proven track record of working in close alignment with internal Clinical Operations teams.

• Experience managing CROs and clinical vendors required.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary compensation range is $215,000 to $270,000, cash bonus, and equity. #LI-Hybrid

jobs.title: Manager, Accounting
jobs.description:
About Us

Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.

It is Kardigan’s mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan’s co-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020.

We have a cutting-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late-stage candidates, and an industry-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

At Kardigan, we are motivated by our values which guide how we work, interact, and achieve our goals. Driven by patients and their families, we are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients and prioritizing their needs above all else. We believe in being authentic—leading with truth to bring out the best in others by creating an environment where every person knows they will be fully accepted. With an eagerness to learn, we encourage the highest levels of curiosity and are open to changing our minds. We are committed to winning as a team with urgency, excellence, and intention, and support each other no matter what role we play or where we sit. Lastly, we strive to enable the impossible because patients are counting on us. We are not afraid to take risks to unlock innovation and advance scientific discoveries.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day.

Position Title: Manager, Accounting

Department: Finance & Accounting

Reports To: Senior Director, Accounting

Location: Princeton, NJ – On-site 4 days per week (Mon to Thurs)

Job Overview

Kardigan is seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Manager, Accounting, to manage and oversee the company’s accounting functions. This position primarily focuses on managing and independently executing complex aspects of the company’s accounting operations, ensuring compliance with GAAP, financial reporting accuracy, and efficient financial processes. In addition, the role will also assist in processing payroll and payroll related matters, accounts payable and purchasing. This is an exciting opportunity for a professional with hands-on experience and a strong accounting background to have a meaningful impact on financial operations within a growing organization. The ideal candidate will play a critical role in driving process improvements and working alongside key internal teams to enhance overall business performance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Accounting Leadership: Manage and oversee the company’s general ledger, ensuring accuracy and compliance with GAAP, internal policies, and regulatory guidelines while leading month-end and year-end close processes, including preparing and reviewing more complex reconciliations, journal entries, and accruals. Own and resolve complex, judgmental balance sheet reconciliations, including R&D and clinical trial expense accruals, prepaid balances, and intercompany accounts, by identifying root causes rather than simply tying out balances. Review and analyze financial data to maintain accuracy and integrity in records, assist in preparing financial statements for business decision-making, and assist with proper accounting treatment, including evaluation of non-routine or judgmental transactions. Research, document, and present the company's position accounting matters (e.g., revenue recognition, leases, R&D cost accrual and capitalization), in clear, well-supported memos.

• System Integration and Management: Lead collaboration with the IT teams to maintain and optimize accounting and payroll systems. Oversee and improve the integration between GL, payroll data, accounts payables, purchasing and the general ledger, and work to enhance the functionality and efficiency of financial systems such as NetSuite, including supporting enhancements that impact multiple functional areas.

• Operational Excellence: Lead continuous improvement initiatives to improve processes and accounting workflows to increase efficiency and scalability, particularly as the organization grows in complexity. Being a reliable backup for the payroll, accounts payable and purchasing functions.

• Audit & Compliance Support: Coordinate accounting and payroll audit activities, ensuring all records and financial reports are accurate, complete, and compliant with applicable laws and regulations. Support the preparation for internal and external audits by providing required documentation and responding to audit inquiries.

• Business Partnership: Work closely with cross-functional teams (HR, IT, FP&A) to provide insights and recommendations that drive operational efficiency and sound financial decision-making, including advising on accounting implications or cross-functional initiatives. Collaborate with the FP&A team to ensure accuracy and integrity in financial reporting. Assemble and prepare statistics on key areas of company operations and assist in analyzing, interpreting, and communicating this information. Serve as a trusted accounting business partner, providing guidance on accounting implications of operational and strategic initiatives.

Qualifications and Preferred Skills

• Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA, or relevant advanced degree preferred.

• 8–10+ years of progressive accounting experience, with at least 2–3 years of experience leading accounting processes, projects, or team members.

• Experience in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or broader life sciences industry, ideally with a pre-commercial or clinical-stage company, is required.

• Strong knowledge of GAAP and payroll regulations, with the ability to interpret and apply this knowledge in financial reporting and payroll transactions.

• Proven ability to exercise independent judgement on complex accounting decisions matters and provide recommendations for financial accuracy and compliance.

• Experience with ERP systems (NetSuite required) Proven ability to design, implement, and improve accounting processes in a growing organization.

• Experience reconciling multiple GL accounts including payroll and benefits.

• Hands-on payroll accounting experience, including booking payroll journal entries (wages, taxes, benefits, and related accruals) and reconciling payroll clearing accounts to the general ledger.

• Experience gathering data for financial and tax audits.

• Ensuring all documentation is audit-ready and policy-compliant, setting standards for the team.

• Some experience with P2P process, with the ability to research transactions and assist team with solutions.

• Experience in working with FP&A on clinical accruals. Understanding the accruals flow for CRO, CMO and other stakeholders, critically analyzing these accruals and ensuring that they are reasonable.

• Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret financial data and ensure accuracy in accounting records.

• You are a self-starter who can plan, organize and take the initiative to meet job objectives and deadlines independently. Ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey financial and payroll information to non-financial stakeholders, including complex topics.

• Demonstrated leadership capabilities, including mentoring team members, leading cross-functional initiatives, and driving process improvements across the organization.

• Experience in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or broader life sciences industry, ideally with a pre-commercial or clinical-stage company, is required.

• Strong fundamental accounting acumen, comfortable working in debits and credits and reasoning through transactions from first principles, with the ability to build or redesign processes rather than simply follow an established one.

• Public accounting experience (e.g., Big 4 or a national/regional firm) and/or experience working within a publicly traded company is a plus.

Exact Compensation may vary based on skills, experience and location.

Pay range

$122,000—$159,000 USD

jobs.title: Senior UX Designer
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

AeroVect is transforming ground handling with autonomy, redefining how airlines and ground service providers around the globe run day-to-day operations. We are a Series A company backed by top-tier venture capital investors in aviation and autonomous driving. Our customers include some of the world’s largest airlines and ground handling providers. For more information, visit www.aerovect.com http://www.aerovect.com.

The Senior User Experience (UX) Designer is responsible for defining the design vision, standards, and execution for AeroVect's Autonomous Ground Support Equipment (AGSE) Service. As AeroVect's first dedicated designer, this role will establish the design function from the ground up - setting the bar for how operators, customers, and internal teams experience our products. The primary focus area will be on Fleet Operations, which covers remote assistance, dispatch, and fleet monitoring interfaces that serve as the operational backbone of the AGSE Service.

Working with the Product team, the Senior UX Designer will own hands-on design for fleet ops surfaces while also setting the design direction for customer-facing tools used by airline and airport stakeholders. This role requires a unique blend of craft, systems thinking, and pragmatism - the ability to design high-information-density operator tools where seconds matter, while also shaping how airline customers interact with the AGSE Service through dashboards, reporting, and SLA visibility. The UX Designer is expected to translate complex autonomy concepts into interfaces that build trust, surface the right information at the right time, and support decision-making across a range of user confidence levels.




YOU WILL

 - Own the design vision and standards for the AGSE Service
   
   - Establish the design principles, patterns, and component library that will scale across fleet operations products and customer-facing tools
   
   - Define the standards for how AeroVect represents autonomy state, system confidence, and exceptions across all user-facing surfaces
   
   - Partner with Engineering on front-end implementation standards to ensure design intent survives the build process
   
   - Set the bar for design quality and review work across the product organization as it grows

 - Lead hands-on design for Fleet Operations products
   
   - Own end-to-end design for remote assistance, dispatch, and fleet monitoring tools - from discovery to high-fidelity execution
   
   - Design for high-stakes, real-time operator workflows where information density, escalation handling, and decision latency directly impact safety and reliability
   
   - Partner with the Fleet Operations Product Manager to translate operator and customer needs into intuitive, scalable interfaces

 - Shape customer-facing experiences
   
   - Design the airline and airport-facing surfaces of the AGSE Service, including operational dashboards, performance reporting, and SLA visibility tools
   
   - Establish a coherent visual and interaction language across operator-facing and customer-facing products, while respecting their different contexts and constraints
   
   - Partner with the Product, Commercial, and Operations teams to ensure customer-facing surfaces reflect the maturity and capability of the underlying service

 - Drive user research and discovery
   
   - Conduct direct research with airline/airport customers and internal operators at active deployments to understand workflows, pain points, and unmet needs
   
   - Establish lightweight research practices that fit the pace of an early-stage company - usability testing, contextual inquiry, and operator shadowing
   
   - Translate research findings into design decisions and product requirements that the broader team can act on


YOU HAVE

 - BFA, BS, or equivalent experience in Design, HCI, or a related field

 - 5+ years of product design experience owning complex, multi-surface products end-to-end

 - Demonstrated experience designing operator-facing or operations tooling - products where users spend hours in the interface and reliability is non-negotiable

 - A strong portfolio showing range across information-dense interfaces, real-time data, and complex workflows

 - Proven ability to ship 0 → 1 products in a fast-paced environment without an established design system to lean on

 - Experience establishing design standards, component libraries, or design systems from scratch

 - Exceptional craft across interaction design, visual design, and information architecture

 - Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to articulate design rationale to technical and non-technical audiences




WE PREFER

 - Experience designing for teleoperations, remote assistance, fleet management, or other real-time monitoring products

 - Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, aviation, industrial operations, or other safety-critical domains

 - Experience as the first designer or early design hire at a startup

 - Familiarity with designing for users operating under time pressure, cognitive load, or safety-critical decision-making

 - Comfort working closely with front-end engineers and contributing to implementation discussions

 - Understanding of how to design interfaces that communicate system confidence, uncertainty, and degraded states

 - Familiarity with airline, airport, or large-scale fleet operations environments

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.



ROLE OVERVIEW

REGENT is building a new category of vehicle that will transform how people and goods move across coastal and maritime environments - creating new possibilities for both commercial transportation and defense missions. Doing that requires a financial foundation built for the realities of a growing hardware and manufacturing company: complex supply chains, multiple R&D programs, increasing production investment, commercial and military customers, and major decisions about where and when to deploy capital.

Following our $240M Series B, we're looking for a Director of Finance to lead our day-to-day Finance function and serve as REGENT's Controller through our next stage of growth. You'll lead the Finance team while staying close to the work yourself — owning accounting, financial planning and modeling, analysis, and reporting while building the financial infrastructure REGENT needs as we prepare for production.

You'll work closely with leaders across REGENT to bring financial context into decisions early and help navigate tradeoffs across programs, headcount, manufacturing investment, CapEx, and other company priorities. You'll also build greater visibility into program and manufacturing economics so we can better understand where we're investing, how we're performing against our plans, and what needs to change as we scale.

This is a build-stage Finance leadership role. As REGENT moves from prototype development toward production, you'll strengthen the financial infrastructure needed for that transition — from planning, accounting, reporting, and controls to manufacturing cost visibility and the financial design and implementation of our ERP.

If you're excited to build and lead a Finance organization through a defining stage of growth, turn ambitious plans into thoughtful financial decisions, and help create the foundation REGENT needs for what comes next, we'd love to meet you.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead the Finance Team: Lead the day-to-day Finance function, setting priorities, developing the team, and building the clarity and accountability needed as REGENT scales.

 - Build Manufacturing & Program Finance: Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Operations, and People to build visibility into program and production economics, including material, labor, overhead, inventory, CapEx, supplier commitments, and product costs.

 - Own Financial Planning & Modeling: Personally build and maintain the models that guide REGENT’s plans and priorities, including budgets, forecasts, cash and runway, scenario planning, program investment, CapEx, and growth.

 - Shape Business & Capital Decisions: Partner with leadership to evaluate investments and tradeoffs across programs, headcount, manufacturing capacity, suppliers, facilities, and other priorities — bringing financial context into decisions early.

 - Own Accounting, Reporting & Audit: Own REGENT’s accounting, close, financial reporting, and first external audit, ensuring the numbers are accurate, defensible, and ready for the board, investors, auditors, and government customers.

 - Lead the ERP Implementation: Own the financial design and implementation of REGENT’s ERP, including chart of accounts, costing, inventory and WIP, procure-to-pay, program accounting, revenue recognition, and reporting.

 - Scale Finance Operations & Controls: Build the systems, processes, and controls needed for a growing manufacturing company — improving speed, visibility, and financial discipline without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Deep Accounting Foundation: You bring strong GAAP fluency, technical accounting judgment, and experience owning the hard questions - not just escalating them. You may have been a Controller, Assistant Controller, or Director of Accounting, or a Finance leader who directly owned the accounting function and was accountable for the technical accounting decisions behind the numbers.

 - Manufacturing Finance Experience: You've led Finance or financial planning in hardware, manufacturing, aerospace, automotive, industrial, or another capital-intensive environment. You understand the realities of building physical products — long development cycles, supply chains, inventory, material and labor costs, CapEx, working capital, and production investment.

 - Strategic & Cross-Functional Leadership: You've partnered closely with executives and functional leaders to turn financial information into decisions. You bring a point of view, challenge assumptions when needed, and can help people who don't live in Finance understand the financial implications of the choices in front of them. You're comfortable owning significant scope while operating as part of a broader team as the company and Finance organization evolve.

 - Audit Experience: You've been through external audits and know what auditors actually ask for, and how to prepare rather than scramble. Taking a company through its first audit is a strong plus.

 - Financial Modeling Depth: You've personally built and owned models that drove meaningful business decisions, including operating plans, cash and runway forecasts, scenario analyses, and investment models. You can move easily between the company-level financial picture and the operational assumptions underneath it.

 - ERP Implementation Experience: You've played a meaningful role in implementing or scaling an ERP and understand the decisions behind processes, data, controls, reporting, and costing — not just the mechanics of implementation. NetSuite experience is a significant advantage.

 - People Leadership: You've led and developed Finance teams, setting clear expectations and creating accountability while giving people the coaching, context, and support they need to grow.

 - Experience Building Through Growth: You've worked in a growing company where the systems, processes, and answers weren't all already in place. You're comfortable walking into ambiguity, figuring out what's needed, and building from there - creating the financial rigor the business needs without slowing it down or adding unnecessary complexity.

 - Genuine Mission Alignment: You're motivated by what REGENT is building, not just the Finance function you'd be running. Seagliders, coastal transportation, defense applications, and the challenge of bringing first-of-a-kind technology into production genuinely interest you — and that comes through in how you engage with the work.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe the best financial decisions are made when Finance understands the business, not when it operates on the sidelines. You build strong relationships across teams, ask the right questions, and help leaders understand the financial implications of their decisions, tradeoffs, and priorities.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You’re comfortable with complex problems that don’t have obvious answers. You dig into the data, challenge assumptions, and bring structure to ambiguity — whether you’re evaluating an investment, improving a forecast, or finding a better way for Finance to support the business.

You see systems, data, automation, and processes as tools for creating better visibility and faster decisions — and you're thoughtful about building infrastructure that can scale with the business rather than simply recreating today's processes in new tools.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, AI Adoption & Growth
jobs.description:
Introduction to Demandbase:

Demandbase is the only pipeline AI platform that empowers GTM teams to automate growth at scale. With a unified view of data, insights, actions, and outcomes, B2B enterprises can seamlessly align and execute their account-based GTM strategies with confidence. Thousands of businesses trust Demandbase to maximize revenue, minimize waste, and consolidate their data and tech stacks – all in one platform. 

As a company, we’re as committed to growing careers as we are to building world-class technology. We invest heavily in people, our culture, and the community around us. We have also continuously been recognized as One of The Best Places To Work in the San Francisco Bay Area by Fortune, and One of The 60 Best Companies To Sell For by Selling Power. Our offices are located in San Francisco, New York, Austin, Seattle, India, and the United Kingdom. 


THE ROLE

Demandbase is accelerating its Agentic Marketing roadmap to bring customers an AI-native platform that performs critical B2B marketing jobs on behalf of marketers. We are looking for a senior product manager to ensure those capabilities do not merely ship; they become trusted, habitual, and monetizable parts of how marketing teams work.

This role will own the customer journey from initial discovery and first value through repeat AI usage, cross-capability adoption, consumption growth, and commercial expansion.




STRATEGIC RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Define the product-led growth strategy for Demandbase’s AI-native application

 - Own the end-to-end adoption funnel across discovery, activation, repeat use, capability composition, AI consumption, and expansion

 - Identify the behaviors that represent meaningful customer value, not merely clicks, sessions, or feature exposure

 - Partner with application PMs to remove friction and introduce the next relevant job or capability at the right moment

 - Design and run product experiments involving onboarding, recommendations, defaults, templates, notifications, approvals, usage visibility, and upgrade paths

 - Develop lifecycle strategies for new customers and existing customers across multiple GTM user personas

 - Partner with Product Analytics and Data Science to establish instrumentation, behavioral cohorts, experimentation methods, and leading indicators of retention and expansion

 - Create reusable growth patterns and platform requirements that can be applied across composable capabilities

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Strong analytical and experimental judgment; able to distinguish correlation from evidence sufficient for a product decision

 - Able to connect customer behavior, qualitative research, product strategy, and commercial outcomes

 - Define activation for each priority JTBD and for the composed product experience

 - Reduce time to first meaningful AI outcome

 - Increase the percentage of active users and tenants completing high-value AI jobs

 - Increase repeat AI use and the number of customers using multiple complementary capabilities

 - Identify which behaviors predict retention, expansion, and increased AI consumption

 - Launch and evaluate experiments that materially improve adoption

 - Help define the product mechanics required for trials, entitlements, credit visibility, and usage-based expansion




WHY THIS ROLE?

This is the ideal role for a high-agency, analytically minded PM who loves turning customer behavior into product decisions and experiments. You won’t just ship AI features; you’ll ensure customers discover them, reach value quickly, build habits around them, and expand into the broader composable platform. You will have the unique opportunity to build the growth engine that turns Demandbase’s AI-native vision into sustained adoption, consumption, retention, and revenue.

This is an entry-level position on the manufacturing floor.  Qualified candidates must be able to perform a variety of jobs, tasks, or duties as required; and must be able to work any shift, overtime, and weekends as required.

• Stack finished products according to established specifications and stacking patterns.
• Inspect finished products for defects, damaged packaging, incorrect labeling, or other quality concerns.
• Remove non-conforming product from the production line and notify the appropriate personnel.
• Maintain a continuous flow of product to prevent production interruptions.
• Safely operate a manual or electric pallet jack to transport finished product, materials, and empty pallets throughout the production area.
• Stage completed product in designated areas for pickup by warehouse personnel.
• Supply empty pallets and other materials to production lines as needed.

• Ability to work in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to product quality.
• Ability to follow written and verbal instructions.

Physical: Must be able to walk throughout the plant, to include walking and climbing up/downstairs and ladders (portable, fixed).  Must have be ability to lift up to 50 pounds occasionally is required.

jobs.description:
Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.

Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!

If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.

Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!

The Engineering team at Lightmatter

The Engineering team at Lightmatter takes photonic computing from research to reality,  overseeing silicon photonics manufacturing, system integration, and 3D Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) development across the full stack, from chip to rack-scale data center deployment.

Responsibilities

Depending on your background, you'll contribute to one or more of these areas:

• Photonics & Silicon Engineering — Support design and simulation of optical components and photonic interconnects that move data at the speed of light.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.location: San Francisco or New York City
jobs.description:
About Pallet

Pallet is building AI Agents to transform the physical economy — a $12 trillion global industry. We’ve raised $50M from top investors, including General Catalyst, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures. In under two years, we’ve achieved 700% revenue growth and are just getting started.

Our mission is to increase the efficiency of the global supply chain by automating the manual workflows that slow supply chain teams down — from scheduling and appointment setting to data entry and load management. Our flagship platform provides end-to-end visibility, control, and optimization, while our newest product, CoPallet, introduces AI Agents that can understand and execute requests in real time and integrate directly with customer systems.

As companies across the physical economy look to generative AI to drive efficiency, many are turning to Pallet to lead the way. With deep supply chain expertise and cutting-edge AI capabilities, we’re positioned to build the next $10B company powering the physical economy.

Join us and work alongside leaders from Google, DoorDash, YC, and more to shape the future of supply chain technology.

$200,000 – $265,000
Full-time / Onsite (5 days/week)

You could be an Infrastructure Engineer anywhere. Why us?

• Join a well-funded, high-growth startup on the path to IPO ($50M raised, 700% revenue growth in 2 years, targeting a $6T market)

• Work directly with the founding engineers who built and still own all of Pallet’s infrastructure

• Help transform a massive, overlooked industry and own the systems that make it possible.

About the opportunity:

Pallet builds AI that runs the physical economy. Freight, warehousing, logistics: the work that actually moves goods around the world. Two-thirds of it still runs on spreadsheets and tribal knowledge, and we’re replacing that with agents that do the real work. The best supply chain teams on the planet already run on us, and they’re pushing us to scale faster than almost anyone our size.

That’s what this role is about. Infrastructure is the thing standing between us and the next order of magnitude, and we’re going all in on it. This person takes on our hardest scaling and reliability problems and owns them outright and sets the technical direction for how Pallet runs at scale.

It’s about as close to a founding infra role as you’ll find at a company that’s already past the risky part. High stakes, real ownership, and a straight line from your work to the business.

Why this role is different:

• You’re one of the first infra hires, so you’ll have huge scope and real ownership.

• We’re pragmatic, lean toward boring, proven technology, and trust engineers to use their judgment.

• The people here are good. That’s the part that’s hard to fake, so come meet the team and see.

How you will make an impact

• Help us scale to millions of AI agent runs per day, solving the capacity, performance, and reliability challenges that come with it.

• Make our platform portable across clouds and on-prem customer environments.

• Work through complex enterprise integration requirements, including identity, private networking, certificate-based authentication, and data residency.

• Own observability and incident response, from alerting and on-call to post-mortems, and make sure the same thing doesn’t break twice.

• Improve developer productivity by making local development, CI, deployments, and production debugging fast and dependable.

Preferred experience

• 5+ years in infrastructure, platform, or SRE roles, ideally at a company or team you joined early and helped scale. Depth and judgment matter more to us than the exact years of experience.

• Real depth in at least one area: databases, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, observability, or application frameworks and runtimes. We value hard-earned production scars over buzzwords.

• A track record of grounding decisions in evidence: setting SLOs, prioritizing performance work, planning capacity, finding bottlenecks, and understanding where systems break.

• Nice to have: some experience with our stack of TypeScript, Postgres, Redis, Google Cloud, OpenTelemetry, and Datadog.

We move fast, and we’ll keep you informed at every stage of the process.

Interview Process

• Chat with Recruiter - 30 mins

• Chat with HM/Technical Screen - 60 mins

• Final Interview - 3-4 hours

• Brief Background Check and Reference Check

Please note: The interview process may vary or shift depending on the role and circumstances.

Compensation

The estimated salary range for this role is $200,000 – $265,000, depending on experience and skill set. In addition to base salary, we offer competitive equity, benefits, and opportunities for growth. Final compensation will be determined based on a combination of factors, including experience, qualifications, and location.

Pallet is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Our Benefits

We invest in our people the same way we invest in our product: seriously.

• 🩺 Health, Vision, and Dental benefits

• 🏝️ Take-what-you-need Paid Vacation

• ➕ Life Insurance and Accidental Insurance

• ❤️‍🩹 Short-Term Disability Coverage

• 💸 Generous salary and equity for all staff

• 🪜 401k option; helping you save for the future

• 🧑‍🧑‍🧒‍🧒 Paid parental leave to support growing families

• 📚 Yearly learning and development stipend

• 🚌 Commuter benefits for Bay Area employees

• 🚘 Uber ride stipend if you ever have to work late in the office

• 🏡 Remote office home stipend to get you comfy in your space

• 🍔 Daily catered lunches provided

• ✈️ Onboarding trip to San Francisco HQ if you work remotely

• 🥤 Monthly happy hours

• 🎉 Annual Company Offsites; our last one was in Palm Springs CA 🌴

Workplace Policy

We are an in-person company. Our offices in San Francisco, New York City and London are where ideas get built, decisions get made, and the team gets stronger. We have invested in making them genuinely great places to spend your day, with catered lunches, monthly happy hours, and people who care about the work and each other.

Most of our team works in office five days a week. For select roles, we hire remotely across the U.S. Remote employees come to one of our offices for their first week to onboard and meet the team, and we cover the full trip.

Every role is different. Travel expectations are always shared upfront in the job description and confirmed in your first call with us.
