jobs.title: Software Engineer, Manufacturing Infrastructure
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We're seeking a Software Engineer to join our First-Party Hardware team. In this role, you will design, build, integrate, and validate the software used to manufacture, qualify, and deliver our hardware from the factory.

You will work across the stack to create the infrastructure that runs internally and externally to coordinate all aspects of the production process. You will create the critical tools and procedures to execute, capture, process, and present the data resulting from the end to end assembly and validation of our hardware across multiple vendors and sites.

This role is hands-on and high-ownership. You will work closely across teams both internal and external to define the standards that will be used across our products to ensure the velocity and quality of our 1P hardware. You will own the implementation, deployment, and output of these systems as well their continued maintenance and SLAs.

Location: San Francisco, CA (Hybrid: 3 days/week onsite). Relocation assistance available.

In this role, you will:

 - Design, develop, and maintain the software infrastructure for manufacturing process execution and data export.

 - Own integration across internal customers and vendor systems and processes.

 - Build and maintain the CI, release, and delivery pipeline of tooling to external partners.

 - Build and maintain internal systems to ingest, process, deliver, and visualize critical data for internal teams and systems.

 - Build system health monitoring, telemetry, remote diagnostics, and recovery paths that make manufacturing failures traceable and actionable.

 - Develop automation frameworks and monitoring for board bring-up, rack bring-up, qualification, manufacturing readiness, deployment readiness, and long-term reliability.

 - Package engineering releases into manufacturing-ready software recipes: images, versions, logs, limits, remediation mapping, provisioning hooks, secure artifact handling, and traceable data export.

 - Debug complex production issues spanning hardware, firmware, kernel, services, networking, power, thermals, boot, provisioning, manufacturing, test, and cloud services.

 - Partner with hardware, firmware, security, networking, infrastructure, manufacturing, operations, and external engineering teams to define software contracts, unblock bring-up, and drive issues to closure.

 - Produce durable architecture notes, runbooks, validation records, and decision documents that help OpenAI and partner teams reproduce, operate, and improve the platform.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 7+ years of hands-on experience, or exceptional accomplishments demonstrating equivalent expertise, in system software, platform software, hardware diagnostics, and cloud infrastructure.

 - Strong programming skills in C, C++, Rust or similar systems languages, with experience building reliable software for real hardware.

 - Familiarity with scripting in languages such as shell and python as used in automation systems.

 - Familiarity with Linux-based hardware platforms, OpenBMC, Redfish, firmware update systems, kernel drivers, and fleet management software.

 - Demonstrated ability to debug live hardware using logs, packet captures, firmware traces, bus captures, lab hosts, BMC journals, Linux tooling, and carefully controlled experiments.

 - Experience with hardware bring-up, manufacturing or qualification testing, system diagnostics, release validation, or deployment of high-performance compute, accelerator, server, networking, storage, or embedded platforms.

 - Ability to reason across software, firmware, hardware, manufacturing, and operations boundaries, and to turn ambiguous problems into clear requirements, designs, tests, and decisions.

 - Proven track record working with external vendors, manufacturing partners, or partner engineering teams to define deliverables, review technical work, and drive issues to closure.

 - Familiarity with platform security topics such as secure boot, firmware signing, device provisioning, attestation, certificate handling, trusted update flows, or access-control design is a plus.

jobs.title: Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

We are seeking a Mechanical Design Engineer to support the development of custom industrial machinery, automation equipment, robotic tooling, and mechanical systems. This role owns mechanical design activities from concept through manufacturing, assembly, testing, and commissioning. The ideal candidate combines strong CAD expertise with hands-on knowledge of fabrication, manufacturing, and automated equipment, while collaborating across engineering and operations teams to deliver reliable, scalable solutions.


Responsibilities

 - Design mechanical systems, machine assemblies, fixtures, tooling, and robotic end-of-arm tooling (EOAT) using 3D CAD software.

 - Create manufacturing drawings, bills of materials, and engineering documentation while applying GD&T and design-for-manufacturing principles.

 - Support fabrication, machining, welding, assembly, prototype builds, and testing activities to ensure successful execution of designs.

 - Collaborate with manufacturing, controls, project management, suppliers, and technicians to develop and improve equipment and processes.

 - Support design reviews, troubleshooting, startup, commissioning, and continuous improvement efforts to optimize performance, reliability, and cost.


Requirements

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.

 - 2+ years of mechanical design experience in industrial, manufacturing, automation, or related environments.

 - Proficiency with SolidWorks or similar 3D parametric CAD software.

 - Understanding of machining, welding, fabrication, assembly processes, engineering drawings, and GD&T.

 - Strong problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills with the ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams.
   

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience designing custom machinery, automation equipment, robotics, fixtures, tooling, or EOAT systems.

 - Experience with pneumatic, hydraulic, vacuum, motion control, or sensor-integrated mechanical systems.

 - Hands-on experience supporting prototype builds, equipment assembly, testing, and commissioning.

 - Familiarity with FEA, engineering analysis tools, or mechanical simulation methods.

 - Experience working in manufacturing, startup, or fast-paced engineering environments.



Compensation

For this role, the target salary range is $120,000 - $165,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees

 - 401k

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.

 - Flexible vacation policy

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

It is the Company’s policy to provide equal employment opportunity for all applicants and employees. jobs.title: Marketplace Operations Manager
jobs.description:
DESCRIPTION

quip is searching for a Marketplace Operations Manager to run and grow our marketplace business. In this role you'll own day-to-day performance across Amazon, TikTok Shop, and 3P marketplaces, and lead the operational launch of every new marketplace quip enters, building the playbook as you go.

You'll be quip's internal expert on every platform we sell on, the day-to-day partner to our Amazon and TikTok Shop agencies, and the link between marketplaces and our creative, marketing, DTC, operations, and CX teams. You'll bring hands-on experience in Amazon Seller Central or TikTok Shop Seller Center, comfortable moving between strategy and execution, and the organization to run several channels at once without dropping a thread.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to our Director, Marketplaces, with scope that grows as quip's marketplace footprint does.

This is a hybrid role based in our DUMBO, Brooklyn office two days per week.

Base Salary: $100k to $120k

This range represents anticipated base salary range for this position, in addition to competitive benefits and equity (as applicable). We carefully assess and consider several factors with each candidate, including location, role-related knowledge, experience and skills. Compensation may vary based on these considerations

RESPONSIBILITIES

Marketplace Operations

• Manage day-to-day execution across Amazon Seller Central, TikTok Shop Seller Center, and other 3P marketplaces, including listings management, promotions, account issue resolution, and other issues as they arise.

• Monitor Buy Box ownership and unauthorized sellers, maintain trackers, and escalate to legal or agency partners as needed.

• Collaborate with the Director of Marketplaces to plan and execute promotional strategy across marketplaces, including alignment with channel counterparts and agencies end-to-end.

• Maintain support files for marketplace operations including item catalog files, promotion calendars, project trackers, and more.

• Own communications with internal and external partners ensuring both are briefed on marketplace plans including innovation launches, promotional event executions, marketing plans, and more

• Serve as the escalation point for marketplace buyer messaging, with agency partners owning day-to-day responses.

Agency Partnership

• Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for quip's Amazon and TikTok Shop agencies.

• Brief agency on deliverables, review the output, and hold agency partners accountable to agreed deadlines and KPIs.

• Translate agency recommendations into decisions the Director and internal teams can act on.

• Facilitate execution of TikTok Shop and Amazon affiliate campaigns and programs with agency partners and social marketing counterparts.

New Marketplace Launches

• Lead the operational build-out of new marketplaces, covering cataloging, content, compliance, and ads setup.

• Act as project manager across internal teams, keeping creative, hardware PM, DTC, operations, and CX aligned to the launch timeline.

• Build repeatable playbooks and SOPs so each launch moves faster than the last.

Listing Quality & Content

• Partner with agencies and internal teams on new launches, including item setup in Amazon Seller Central.

Inventory & Demand Signal

• Oversee the demand planning process by monitoring inventory health across marketplaces, providing demand input to agencies for file updates, flagging stockout risk early, and representing marketplaces in internal demand planning meetings.

• Partner with agencies and Operations on shipment planning so inventory levels support sales targets.

• Own the marketplace forecast for new item launches, aligning inputs with the Director and partnering with hardware PMs through launch.

Performance & Insights

• Own the read on marketplace performance across sales, ad spend and efficiency, conversion, content health, and inventory, and proactively flag risks and opportunities.

• Interrogate Amazon and TikTok Shop advertising performance across campaigns including Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Sponsored Display, and hold agency partners accountable to the plan.

REQUIREMENTS

jobs.title: Director - Global Talent Management
jobs.description:
Freshworks is rethinking how we develop, evaluate, and listen to our people — and this role is at the center of that transformation. As Director of Performance Management & Employee Listening, you will lead two of our most strategically important people practices: a comprehensive redesign of how we approach performance management, and a shift to a modern, continuous approach to employee listening.

This is a role for someone who thinks systemically, designs with the business in mind, and cares about execution as much as strategy. Ultimately, you are helping us build something lasting: a sustainable culture of high performance and an employee experience that is genuinely differentiated. You will work as part of a small, senior Workforce Strategy & Org Development team — owning your domain with a high degree of autonomy and leading through influence across a matrixed organization. You will not manage a large team, but you will need to move a lot of work through people who don't report to you.

Based at our San Mateo headquarters, you will work alongside senior leaders and represent the People team in high-visibility conversations at the VP and executive level. We need someone who commands a room, earns trust quickly, and brings both creative thinking and rigorous follow-through to everything they own. Critically, you know that even the best-designed programs fail without deliberate change management — and you build enablement, communication, and adoption into your work from the start.

What You’ll Do

Performance Management Transformation

• Lead a meaningful transformation of how Freshworks approaches performance management — moving from a process-heavy, subjective model to a streamlined, AI-assisted approach that is easier for managers, more consistent in its outputs, and more tightly connected to business outcomes.
• Design and own the end-to-end performance system: the methodology, the tools, the calibration approach, and the employee and manager experience.
• Coordinate across HR, Total Rewards, HR Technology, and business partners to deliver an integrated solution that actually works in practice.
• Build and maintain executive alignment. This work is visible to senior leadership, and you will present, defend, and iterate on it in real time.
• Lead the change management and enablement strategy for the performance transformation — developing communications, training, and leader readiness plans that drive understanding and adoption across the organization.
• Hold the bar on quality and detail at every stage.

Employee Listening

• Own our employee listening strategy and programs, including our continuous listening platform, pulse approach, and how we translate signals into leadership action.
• Drive the shift from periodic survey cycles to an always-on listening culture — designing and executing the change management strategy that moves leaders from passive recipients of survey results to active owners of the employee feedback loop.
• Build leader-facing tools, frameworks, and communications that make listening data accessible and useful, not just reportable.
• Track program health, participation trends, and sentiment over time; surface risks and opportunities and bring forward clear recommendations.
• Stand up and lead a cross-functional employee experience working group — bringing together leaders from People Analytics, Employee Experience, and the HRBP community to build a cohesive, multi-lens view of the state of the employee experience. This group will be responsible for maturing how we aggregate and interpret employee signals, and for delivering a regular, centralized view of organizational health to senior leadership.
• Continuously improve our approach as AI capabilities and listening methodologies evolve

Change Management & Enablement

• Own the change management and enablement strategy across both performance and listening — from how we communicate program shifts to how we build leader capability and drive adoption at scale. The goal is not compliance with new programs; it is durable behavior change that builds a culture of high performance and an employee experience people can feel.
• Apply behavioral science principles to the design of change interventions — using what we know about habit formation, social norms, loss aversion, and motivation to design programs that shift behavior, not just awareness.
• Design and deliver leader enablement programs that translate program changes into concrete behaviors: what leaders need to know, do, and model differently as a result of each transformation.
• Build a communication and engagement framework that keeps employees, managers, and senior leaders informed, aligned, and bought in throughout multi-year transformation cycles.
• Serve as the connective tissue between program design and organizational readiness — ensuring that what we build in the design room actually lands in the field.
• Measure adoption and enablement effectiveness; use data to identify where uptake is lagging and adjust approach accordingly.

• 8–12 years of progressive experience in HR, people strategy, organizational effectiveness, or a related field.
• Proven experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation initiatives from design through execution in a fast-paced environment. • Deep expertise in performance management design — you’ve built or significantly redesigned performance systems before and understand how to make them fair, scalable, and defensible.
• Meaningful experience in organizational design and development — you can help leaders think through structure and effectiveness, and you know how to turn those conversations into action.
• Strong change management and enablement skills — you know how to bring people along through transformation, build leader capability, and design adoption strategies that actually stick. • Familiarity with continuous listening platforms and methodology; experience driving leader adoption of listening tools is a strong plus.
• An AI-first mindset — you’re curious about what AI makes possible in people practices and you bring that perspective to how you design programs and solve problems.
• Exceptional executive presence — you’re comfortable presenting to C-suite leaders, you communicate with clarity and confidence, and you can hold your own in high-stakes rooms.
• High attention to detail — you care deeply about getting things right and you’ll get into the weeds to make sure they are. • Strong cross-functional instincts — you build trust with Finance, Strategy, and Operations partners and you design solutions that work for the business, not just for HR. • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; you can translate complexity into clarity for any audience.

jobs.title: Risk Officer
jobs.description:
Webull is a leading digital brokerage platform built on next generation global infrastructure. At Webull, we believe that everyone should have an equal opportunity to control their own financial future. Our vision has always been to empower individual investors with the tools and resources they need to succeed financially. This commitment remains at the heart of everything we do. From low-fee trading and robust market data to advanced analytical tools, we are committed to providing a seamless, top-tier trading experience.

About The Role & Team

At Webull, we are committed to empowering individual investors with the tools and resources they need to take control of their finances.  Our mobile-first platform provides commission-free trading of stocks, options, and ETFs, giving users the freedom to invest in the assets that matter to them without worrying about high fees eating into their returns. In March 2024, we announced our addition of futures trading.

Webull Futures LLC operates in a highly regulated futures environment where disciplined risk governance, strong controls, and proactive regulatory engagement are essential. The risk function is responsible for identifying, measuring, monitoring, and escalating the financial, operational, liquidity, credit, market, technology, and third-party risks associated with the firm’s futures business.

We are seeking a senior, highly experienced Risk Officer for Webull Futures LLC. This individual will be the senior-most risk officer for the futures business and will own the design, implementation, and ongoing oversight of the firm’s risk management framework. The role will partner closely with executive leadership, Compliance, Legal, Operations, Product, Treasury, Finance, Technology, and enterprise risk leadership to ensure that Webull Futures LLC maintains a robust, scalable, and regulator-ready risk program aligned with CFTC, NFA, exchange, clearing, and internal governance expectations.

In This Role, You Will

• Serve as the senior-most risk officer for Webull Futures LLC, with ownership of the firm’s futures risk management framework, governance structure, policies, procedures, limits, reporting, and escalation protocols.
• Identify, assess, monitor, and escalate material risks across the futures business, including market, credit, liquidity, operational, technology, model, vendor, clearing, margin, concentration, and regulatory risk.
• Establish and oversee risk appetite, key risk indicators, trading and exposure limits, stress testing, scenario analysis, margin monitoring, and other risk controls appropriate for an FCM and technology-driven futures platform.
• Partner with the CEO of Webull Futures LLC, US CRO, Compliance, Legal, Operations, Product, Treasury, Finance, Technology, and enterprise risk leadership to ensure risk considerations are embedded into strategy, product development, operational processes, and new business initiatives.
• Provide independent risk challenge and executive-level guidance on futures product launches, client onboarding, clearing relationships, margin policy, liquidity planning, incident management, and business continuity preparedness.
• Prepare and present risk reports, dashboards, escalations, and governance materials to senior management, board-level stakeholders, committees, and relevant control functions.
• Maintain a regulator-ready risk program and support interactions with the CFTC, NFA, exchanges, clearing organizations, auditors, and other external stakeholders in coordination with Compliance and Legal.
• Stay informed of futures industry developments, regulatory expectations, market structure changes, and emerging risks, and proactively evolve the risk program as Webull Futures LLC scales.

The Skills You Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, risk management, accounting or a related quantitative field; an advanced degree or relevant professional certification is preferred.
• Minimum of 8+ years of progressive risk management experience in futures, derivatives, clearing, FCM, broker-dealer, exchange, financial technology, or similarly regulated financial services environments.
• Demonstrated experience serving in a senior risk leadership, senior risk officer, head of risk, or equivalent control-function leadership role with direct exposure to executive management and governance bodies.
• Deep understanding of risk management practices applicable to futures and derivatives businesses, including margin, liquidity, market risk, operational resilience, clearing, client exposure, concentration risk, stress testing, and escalation frameworks.
• Strong familiarity with CFTC, NFA, exchange, clearinghouse, and related regulatory expectations, with experience supporting examinations, inquiries, audits, or regulatory interactions.
• Proven ability to build, scale, and mature a risk management program in a fast-paced, technology-driven financial services organization.

What Makes You Stand Out

• Excellent executive communication skills, including the ability to present concise risk assessments, recommendations, and escalations to senior management, boards, committees, regulators, and cross-functional stakeholders.
• Strong judgment, independence, analytical rigor, and commercial awareness, with the ability to provide effective challenge while enabling responsible business growth.
• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, technology-focused environment, with a proactive, data-driven, and forward-looking approach to risk management.

Why Webull?

Webull is more than a fintech company—we’re a global community of innovators, collaborators, and trailblazers. Headquartered in St. Petersburg, FL, Webull operates in 16 regions worldwide, serving over 20 million users. At Webull, your ideas matter, your voice is heard, and your work makes a real impact.

Investing in our people is a top priority for us, which is why we have a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

• Comprehensive Health Coverage: 100% paid medical and dental insurance for employees and dependents, vision insurance, and more!
• Financial Support: 401(k) match, commuter benefits for NY positions, and short-term disability coverage.
• Work-Life Balance: Generous time off that increases with tenure, paid parental leave, personal days, sick time, volunteer days and company holidays.
• Wellness & Pet Care: Fitness and wellness benefits, plus pet insurance for your furry friends.
• Investing in Your Future: We provide tuition reimbursement to help you pursue relevant degrees, certifications, and training that align with your career goals.
• Dynamic Office Perks: Catered breakfast (every Monday) & lunches (every Friday), fully stocked kitchens, and monthly happy hours to connect and collaborate.

This role is based in our New York Office (44 Wall Street), where in-person collaboration fuels growth, mentorship, and innovation. At Webull, we’re committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation. The base salary range is ($135,000 - $165,000) annually, plus a discretionary bonus and full benefits. Final offers consider experience, location, and relevant qualifications.

EEOC Statement

Webull is an equal opportunity employer. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team where all backgrounds, perspectives, and talents are valued.

jobs.description:
As a Chemical Operator, you will play a crucial role in the safe and efficient operation of our chemical manufacturing processes. You will be responsible for monitoring and controlling equipment, performing quality checks, and ensuring compliance with safety and environmental regulations. Your attention to detail and adherence to standard operating procedures will contribute to the production of high-quality chemicals. As part of this role, you will also serve as a member of the Emergency Response Team (ERT).

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

• Support all Environmental, Health, and Safety programs, policies, and regulations to include the issuance of safe work permits (LOTO, hot work, etc.).
• Make necessary adjustments to equipment units affecting speeds of chemical reactions and quality.
• Monitor recording instruments, flow meters, panel lights, and other indicators, and listen for warning signals, to verify conformity of process conditions.
• Control or operate chemical processes or systems of machines, using panel boards, control boards, or automatic equipment. Record operating data such as process conditions and instrument readings.
• Confer with technical and supervisory personnel to report or resolve conditions affecting safety, efficiency, and product quality. Draw samples of products to be tested in the lab to ensure that standards are met.
• Regulate or shut down equipment during emergency situations or as directed by supervisory personnel.
• Start pumps to wash and rinse reactor vessels, to exhaust gases and vapors, to regulate the flow of oil, steam, air or gas to towers and to add products to converter or blending vessels.
• Notify maintenance, engineering and other auxiliary personnel to correct equipment malfunctions and to adjust power, steam, water or air supplies as needed.
• Inspect and operate Utility Equipment such as towers, boilers, chillers and scrubbers.
• Calculate material requirements or yields according to formulas as directed. Gauge tank levels, using calibrated rods and pressure gauges.
• Serve as an Emergency Response Team member in the event of an emergency.
• Responding to all emergency events, including fire, chemical spill/release, medical events, severe weather events, etc.

MINIMUM POSITION QUALIFICATIONS

• High School Graduate or General Education Degree (GED)
• Minimum of 1-2 years’ experience working in a chemical manufacturing environment with hazardous materials.
• Experience driving a forklift

EXPERIENCE

• Minimum of 2 years’ related experience within the manufacturing / chemical industry.
• Excellent communication and documentation skills
• Attention to detail and strong math skills
• Strong computer skills, including MS Outlook, Excel, Word, and the Internet
• Team player, individual thinker
• Customer focused; positive attitude

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Associate Degree in Process Technology or equivalent preferred.
• Attention to detail and numbers-oriented
• Excellent communication and documentation skills
• Strong computer skills
• Working knowledge of SAP
• Team player, individual thinker
• Previous experience dealing with HAZMAT, Fire, and/or Medical emergency events

Physical Requirements

• This position requires successful completion of a medical surveillance examination as a condition of employment.
• Ability to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) (Safety Boots, Safety Clothing, Safety Helmet, Safety Goggle/Glasses, Respirator, Gloves)

jobs.title: Electrical Project Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Ground Systems Deployment Team

The Ground Systems Deployment and Construction team is responsible for turning bare ground into functional drone charging sites! We’re a broad, cross-functional team with skills across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, and construction engineering with a mandate to deliver world-class construction execution with zero issues in the first 30 days, on-time and on-budget, using scalable, cost-optimized, and serviceable designs.

The Role

The Ground System Deployment and Construction Engineering team is seeking a curious, collaborative Electrical Engineering Intern to support the design and deployment of Zipline’s Ground Systems across a variety of sites and applications.

In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience with commercial and light-industrial electrical distribution as applied to an autonomous drone delivery network. Working alongside experienced engineers, you’ll help with utility coordination, site-level electrical design, structure-level wiring approaches, and technical documentation.

You’ll collaborate with mechanical, structural, electrical, and deployments teams to support real-world projects and contribute to problem-solving as new challenges arise. This internship also offers opportunities to explore new design ideas and assist with improvements to our engineering processes. You’ll work and become familiar with the National Electrical Code and apply the concepts to site and infrastructure designs.

The internship is based in South San Francisco, with occasional travel within California and the U.S. for site visits or field support.

What You'll Do

• Support engineers with research, drafting, and documentation for electrical distribution and structure-level wiring designs aligned with NEC and relevant standards.

• Assist with UL/TUV certification efforts by gathering documentation, preparing technical materials, and coordinating with engineering partners.

• Help prepare materials, track communication, and support interactions with deployment and construction teams

• Implement feedback from Deployment and Construction teams to continuously optimize designs for more efficient build and scale

• Design electrical distribution of commercial and light industrial ground system projects per NEC and relevant applicable codes and standards.

• Design next generation charging structure level electrical wiring and installation approaches.

• Evaluate all options and a lean budget, select best vendors to ensure reliable and quality services and products.

• Help document project risks, prepare materials for meetings, support communication across teams, and occasionally participate in site visits for field observations.

• Create documentation to ensure quality and process refinement between each build to help with consistent scale

• Collaborate with engineering and business teams to understand customer needs and contribute to improvements in Ground Systems infrastructure.

• Travel to commercial and flight test sites may be required on an ad hoc basis.

What You'll Bring

• You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies, with relevant coursework (e.g., circuits, power systems, construction). Master's and PhD students are also eligible.

• Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and a willingness to ask questions and learn.

• Familiarity with engineering tools or concepts such as CAD/ECAD, electrical modeling, or basic simulation software. (Revit, Bluebeam Revu, AutoCAD, NX)

• Clear written and verbal communication skills, especially when summarizing technical information.

• Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment and support a wide range of tasks.

• Curiosity, initiative, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. Comfort with hands-on work and openness to occasional travel (if needed).

• An open mind to help us bring Zipline’s service to new and existing customers!

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September).

The hourly rate for this internship is $44 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

jobs.description:
POSITION DURATION:

This is a six-month contract role located in San Carlos with the potential to extend or convert to full-time based on performance and business needs.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Research Associate 1/2 performs laboratory procedures of varying complexity contributing to cross functional activities as part of the RUO Oncology Team, a multidisciplinary team within the research and development department.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Normalize plasma samples.

• Extract nucleic acids from whole blood, plasma, tissue blocks using automated and manual extraction methods

• Perform library preparation for nextgen sequencing using automated and manual methods

• Determine quantity and/or quality of nucleic acids using Quant-IT, Qubit, Nanodrop, BioAnalyzer, and qPCR

• Load libraries onto next generation sequencing platforms ( NovaSeq, iSeq,, Miseq, etc)

• Interpret data and determine appropriate next steps per outlined requirements

• Perform routine laboratory equipment maintenance as defined in standard operating procedures

• Recognize equipment and instrument malfunctions and escalate to R&D equipment support team and relevant team members

• Track sample inventory and status using Laboratory Information Management Software or Google Sheets

• Maintain accurate records of lab work using a variety of softwares including Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, and internal databases

• Periodically review standard operating procedures (SOP) and other work instructions

• Suggest process improvements to subject matter experts as needed

• Ensure accurate, ethical, and appropriate management of samples in compliance with all applicable federal regulation

• Perform other tasks as specified by the manager/director

• This role occasionally works with PHI both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job

• Employees must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire

• Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements

• Employee must pass post offer criminal background check

• Additional requirement: This role requires onsite work in San Carlos and flexibility to work shifted schedules (e.g., 7am - 4pm, 11am - 8pm, 7pm - 3am)

QUALIFICATIONS:

• BS/BA in a biological science or equivalent required

• 1-3 years of related laboratory experience

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

• Extremely familiar with good pipetting practices (single and multi-channel micropipettes, serological pipettes)

• Hands-on experience with library preparation and next generation sequencing platforms highly preferred (NovaSeq, MiSeq, iSeq etc.)

• Hands-on experience with nucleic acid techniques (purification, quantification, amplification, etc)

• Able to operate independently in lab under general supervision with minimal human error

• Knowledge of LIMS/database softwares

• Experience with laboratory automation is a plus

• Excellent with Microsoft Office programs

• Excellent with Google Drive including Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Forms

• Excellent oral and written communication skills

• Ability to think creatively and analytically with strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills

• Team player with demonstrated strong interpersonal skills with an ability to build effective working relationships within functional area

• Ability to thrive in a fast paced, evolving environment, and manage competing priorities efficiently

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:

• Duties are typically performed in an office and laboratory setting daily

• This position requires the ability to perform repetitive motions during pipetting and sample processing

• This position requires the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone and read printed material

• May require lifting or moving items weighing up to 25lbs.

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. jobs.title: QA Software Engineer (Remote)
jobs.description:
QA SOFTWARE ENGINEER (REMOTE)

 

Building the Quality Standard for Veterinary Care Infrastructure

Nest Veterinary is on track to 5X this year. We’re the category leader in care plan infrastructure for veterinary practices, and our continued growth depends on building an exceptional team. As our first dedicated Quality hire, you’ll play an important role in defining how quality works at Nest — building the test infrastructure, AI-assisted workflows, and reliability standards that let us ship fast and with confidence as we scale. If you love automation-first testing, AI-assisted workflows, and owning quality end-to-end across a full stack, this could be a great fit for you.



ABOUT NEST VETERINARY

Our mission is simple: make pet care accessible to every pet parent. We provide fully managed, tech-enabled care plan solutions that help veterinary practices increase compliance, drive revenue, and deliver better preventive care without the administrative burden.

We’re transforming an industry with design-forward products, thoughtful technology, and a team that cares deeply about the work we’re building together.



THE ROLE

 

What You'll Own

Build Test Coverage Across the Stack

Architect and build a robust test suite from the ground up for our Flutter applications (web + desktop) and our FastAPI/gRPC backend services. Build contract and integration tests for critical APIs, including payment processing, PIMS integrations, and internal services.

Pioneer AI-Assisted QA

Use LLMs to generate test cases from PRs, specs, and code diffs, then curate and maintain the output. Use AI for exploratory testing — feeding app state, API responses, and UI structures into models to surface edge cases and inconsistencies humans would miss. Build and maintain prompt libraries and workflows for repeatable AI-assisted QA tasks.

Own Production Reliability

Own observability from a quality and reliability lens: error budgets, alerting thresholds, anomaly detection, and resilience testing. Instrument visual regression testing for our admin and hospital-facing UIs.

Build Quality Infrastructure & Process

Develop and maintain test data management strategies and reusable test utilities. Establish defect reporting and triage workflows, and quality metrics/reporting, so the rest of engineering has a clear view of coverage and release readiness.

Partner Across the Org

Collaborate with developers, product, and customer support to identify quality risks early, with a customer-first mindset toward the end-to-end experience. Work with developers to improve test patterns across the codebase, with a bias toward generated-and-reviewed over hand-written-from-scratch. Continuously evaluate new AI testing tools and integrate them where they create real leverage.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 

 - 3+ years in a QA, SDET, or test automation role — automation-first, not manual-first

 - Active, demonstrated use of AI/LLM tools in your testing and reliability workflow (Claude, Copilot, Codex, or similar) — we will ask you about this in detail

 - Strong proficiency in Dart and Flutter testing (unit, widget, golden, and integration tests)

 - Experience testing Flutter Web (Playwright or similar) and/or Flutter Desktop applications strongly preferred

 - Comfort writing Python tests for FastAPI and gRPC services (pytest experience a big plus)

 - Experience building CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, or similar)

 - Comfort working across the stack — Flutter frontends, Python/gRPC backends, and third-party integrations

 - Experience with contract testing or API testing frameworks

 - Familiarity with production observability tools (Sentry, Datadog, or similar) and reliability concepts like SLOs and error budgets

 - Strong product intuition — able to identify the 10% of paths that carry 90% of the risk

 - Self-directed and comfortable building a function from zero, not inheriting one


WHY NEST

 

 - 5X growth trajectory — your work will directly contribute to how Nest grows and scales

 - High-impact role — you’ll have meaningful ownership and the opportunity to make a visible impact across the business

 - Mission that matters — help more pets get access to the preventive care they need

 - Ground-floor opportunity — help define what great quality and reliability engineering looks like as Nest continues to grow

 - Teammates who show up — work alongside a kind, motivated, and collaborative team

 

Nest is an equal-opportunity employer. You are welcome at Nest for who you are, no matter where you come from or what you look like. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. Bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It's in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing veterinary health care and help pets live longer, healthier, and happier lives.

jobs.title: Network Engineer
jobs.description:
WE ARE AN APPLIED AI LAB BUILDING END-TO-END SOFTWARE AGENTS.

We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer. 

Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro.

Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Network Engineer to own the reliability, security, and evolution of Cognition’s global office

networks.

Strong candidates have operated networks in a hypergrowth startup and thrive amid rapid change, ambiguity, and high ownership. They will apply deep wireless and routing expertise and a builder mindset to deliver scalable wired, wireless, and cloud-connected networks, repeatable office infrastructure, and strong observability and automation. Working across internal teams, carriers, and partners, they will own outcomes end to end and continuously improve the network through stakeholder feedback and operational data.

This role is onsite five days a week. We value teamwork and in-person collaboration.




WHAT YOU’LL DO


OWN SCALABLE NETWORKS AND OFFICE DELIVERY

 - Design, deploy, and operate high-performance wired and wireless networks across offices, branches, and large campus environments, including RF optimization and resilient architectures using technologies such as VLANs, LACP, OSPF, BGP, VRFs, QoS, and redundant internet and core paths.

 - Own network delivery for offices, expansions, and moves—from procurement, circuit turn-up, and vendor coordination through cutover and handoff—and, as Cognition scales, build secure connectivity across offices, cloud infrastructure, and Devin environments using VPC peering, transit networking, IPsec, GRE, or SD-WAN.

 - Create repeatable reference architectures, configuration and lifecycle standards, high-availability patterns, capacity models, inventories, diagrams, runbooks, and deployment playbooks for a growing global footprint.
   
   
   
   BUILD OBSERVABLE AND AUTOMATED NETWORK OPERATIONS

 - Own network monitoring and observability across availability, performance, capacity, and employee experience, using telemetry and analytics to identify degradation before customers report it.

 - Develop scripts, reusable tooling, and data pipelines in Python, Go, TypeScript, or another modern language to improve reliability and turn network data into actionable insight.

 - Apply infrastructure-as-code, APIs, source control, and CI/CD to automate network configuration and deployment.

 - Use Devin and AI to improve network reliability, building the skills, context, and runbooks needed for effective troubleshooting and automation.
   
   
   
   SECURE ACCESS AND SERVE OUR STAKEHOLDERS

 - Implement secure, identity-aware network access, segmentation, certificate-based authentication, and least-privilege infrastructure administration.

 - Partner with Security on firewalls, threat detection and prevention, secure remote access, and incident response.

 - Troubleshoot systematically across the OSI model, using packet analysis and telemetry to isolate root causes across clients, RF, switching, routing, applications, and external providers.

 - Build trusted relationships with stakeholders, listen to their experience, communicate clearly during incidents, and continuously improve rather than accepting that the network is “good enough.”
   


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience designing, deploying, and operating enterprise or campus networks, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Experience building and operating networks in a hypergrowth startup, with a track record of thriving amid rapid change, ambiguity, and high ownership.

 - A bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, network engineering, or a related discipline—or equivalent practical experience.

 - Demonstrated depth in wireless RF engineering and enterprise switching and routing, including successful delivery of branch offices or large office environments.

 - Strong knowledge of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, Ethernet, Wi-Fi, routing protocols, VPN and zero-trust remote access technologies such as Cloudflare WARP, and structured troubleshooting across the OSI model.

 - Experience designing for high availability, fault isolation, capacity, and scale across critical network services and connectivity paths.

 - Experience with network performance monitoring, telemetry, alerting, and analytics, with a track record of using operational data to improve reliability or customer experience.

 - Experience automating network operations with a modern programming or scripting language and applying APIs, infrastructure-as-code, Git, or CI/CD to configuration delivery.

 - Working knowledge of network security and identity controls, including IEEE 802.1X, NAC, AAA, RBAC, segmentation, IDS/IPS, or related technologies.

 - Experience coordinating carriers, contractors, and vendors while maintaining clear internal ownership of architecture, quality, documentation, and outcomes.

 - Strong judgment, communication, and service orientation, with a track record of carrying ambiguous problems through design, implementation, and ongoing operation.


AN IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL BRING

 - Ownership: Treats reliability and customer experience as personal responsibilities, drives ambiguous work through completion, and remains accountable across team and vendor boundaries.

 - Customer focus: Seeks direct feedback, translates user experience into technical improvements, and recognizes that a technically operational network may still be failing its customers.

 - Builder mindset: Solves immediate issues while improving architecture, automation, observability, documentation, and operating practices to prevent recurrence.

 - Curiosity: Continually tests assumptions, learns new technologies, and explores practical ways to use AI to improve network reliability, visibility, and engineering effectiveness.


BONUS POINTS

 - High-density wireless, modern Wi-Fi, or large multi-site campuses.

 - IaaS cloud networking in AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure.

 - Advanced routing, SD-WAN, SASE, or hybrid-cloud connectivity.

 - Network telemetry and analytics using NetFlow/IPFIX, gNMI, or similar tools.

 - Automation using NetBox, Ansible, Terraform, or similar platforms.

 - Applying AI or AIOps to reliability, capacity planning, or incident response.

 - CCNP Enterprise, CWNP, or equivalent demonstrated technical depth.


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Cognition is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process - please let us know if you need any.

jobs.title: Deployment Strategist, Flagship Account
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Serval http://serval.com is an AI-native automation platform transforming how enterprises operate. We build intelligent agents that understand real-world workflows and execute them end-to-end — replacing manual processes and rigid legacy systems with adaptive, learning software. Founded in early 2024, Serval is already trusted by companies like Fox, Notion, Perplexity, Vercel, and Brex to automate high-volume, high-friction operational work across their organizations.

At the core of Serval is an agentic AI platform that turns natural language into production-grade workflows. Our agents don’t just respond to requests — they reason, take action across systems, and continuously improve with usage. What began with operational use cases has quickly evolved into a horizontal AI automation layer used across IT, HR, Finance, Security, Legal, and Engineering.

Our mission is to eliminate repetitive, manual work across the enterprise and give teams leverage through intelligent automation. Long term, we’re building the universal AI operations layer — a system of agents that sits across business functions and runs the workflows that keep modern companies moving.

We’re backed by leading investors including Sequoia Capital, Redpoint Ventures, Meritech, First Round, General Catalyst, Elad Gil, and others. 




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Agent Deployment team is a customer-facing technical team, central to how Serval turns product capability into real business outcomes. The org is a family of roles: Deployment Strategists are the primary technical relationship and AI advisor for each customer, partnering with Deployed Software Engineers to build enterprise-grade features and products. Deployment Success Managers own each customer's long-term success, building the systems and motions that scale adoption, expansion, and renewal well past go-live.



ROLE OVERVIEW

This role is dedicated to one of Serval's largest and most strategic customers (one of the largest companies in the world). You'll work in a hybrid model, spending a few days each week embedded alongside the customer's team in Santa Clara and the remainder of your time working with the Serval team at our San Francisco HQ.

As a Deployment Strategist on Serval's Agent Deployment team, you’ll be the primary technical relationship for Serval’s customers: guiding their deployments, advising their AI strategy, and owning their outcomes. You’ll work deeply within Serval’s existing product surface area: building novel workflows, configuring integrations, and shipping bug fixes and product changes yourself.

This role is for someone who thrives on execution velocity, moving quickly across multiple engagements at once. You’re at home in ambiguity and bring a strong blend of technical depth, product sense, and customer obsession. And because you sit closest to how customers actually use Serval, you'll directly shape our product roadmap: the workflows and features you build in the field make their way into the core product.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own customer engagements from pilot through production launch: design and deliver deployments that fit the customer's workflows and scale adoption of Serval.

 - Build AI agents: design and build AI agents on Serval's platform that drive real value for customers.

 - Advise AI strategy: embed with customers to guide and shape how they adopt and scale AI.

 - Lead migrations: design and execute migration plans that minimize disruption and ensure seamless adoption of Serval's platform.

 - Partner cross-functionally: work with Engineering, Sales, and Marketing to turn field learnings into repeatable processes and a sharper go-to-market.




WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - 3+ years in a relevant role (product, engineering, consulting, founder).

NICE TO HAVE

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Impact: Be a key player in shaping the success of our product and company.

 - Growth: Build a fundamentally new AI product offering with the support of our experienced team and investors. Grow rapidly with the company.

 - Culture: Join a culture that values innovation, ownership, accountability, and fun.

jobs.title: Senior Radar Engineer, Air Defense
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Air Defense team builds autonomous robots that find other robots and knock them out of the sky. This team is the nexus of premier Anduril-built products such as Roadrunner, Sentry, Anvil, Pulsar, and Wisp integrated into a software-enabled Air Defense family of systems tailored to the modern battle-space. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, we provide critical force protection capabilities to support the warfighter. Our autonomous family of networked sensors and effectors enables our users to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of UAS threats that continue to evolve at a rapid pace.

ABOUT THE JOB

Detecting a small, fast, low-flying drone is the hardest problem in the counter-UAS kill chain, and everything downstream depends on getting it right. We are looking for a Senior Radar Engineer to join our rapidly growing Air Defense team based in Irvine, CA. In this role, you will own the architecture, performance, and detection and tracking performance of networked radar systems that feed our family of systems, working alongside effector, autonomy, and Lattice teams to turn a raw detection into a closed kill chain. This will require deep radar systems expertise, the judgment to make hard performance trades against real threat sets, and the willingness to stay hands-on from sensor performance through field integration.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Architect and implement RF sensing technologies for air defense radar systems and multi-domain platforms

• Conduct rigorous system-of-systems analysis to decompose operational requirements into radar subsystem specifications, link budgets, and performance trades

• Work with our internal and external radars to validate advanced radar techniques, waveforms, signal processing algorithms, and detection/tracking technologies against evolving UAS threats

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define system architectures and concepts of operations for networked sensor and effector engagements

• Create and drive consensus on internal technical roadmaps for counter-UAS radar capabilities

• Engage directly with DoD customers to translate operational needs into technical requirements

• Provide technical leadership to program management and business development teams to support strategic decision-making

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• BS or MS degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or related technical field, and 5+ years of hands-on experience in radar systems engineering, including hardware, algorithms, or software development

• Strong expertise in radar architecture, waveform design, radar modes, and system-level modeling

• Proficiency in MATLAB and Python for radar simulation and analysis

• Proven track record in a technical leadership role developing high-performance defense radar systems

• Must be authorized to work in the United States

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Hands-on experience developing RF sensing systems for detection and tracking of small, low-observable, low-altitude targets

• Proficiency in C++ for real-time embedded systems or signal processing pipelines

• Understanding of radar antenna development, technology, and integration

• Prior experience supporting DoD or IC programs

US Salary Range

$146,000—$194,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Research Tools
jobs.description:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on the RL Data team, you’ll design and build the tools that researchers and external contributors use to create, review, submit, and monitor the environments and tasks behind Cursor’s reinforcement-learning runs. This is a full-stack product-engineering role embedded in a research team.

You’ll own the review and acceptance experience end to end: from rollout and transcript inspection, task-quality signals grader and reward-hacking analysis, to the workflows that move a submission into training. From there, you’ll build authoring interfaces that let researchers, vendors, and domain experts create and improve environments and tasks quickly and confidently.

Your work will significantly shorten the loop from a task idea or data sources, to candidate task, to trusted training data.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

 - Create fast, trustworthy workflows for vendors and research team to interact effectively with each other — vendor task creation and iteration, vendor submissions, and task acceptance into training.

 - Build review tools for inspecting and comparing rollouts, transcripts, grader outputs, and other signals of task quality.

 - Develop environment-health, failure-search, versioning, and catalog experiences that make training data easy to understand, manage, and extend.

 - Establish a shared component kit, then use it to build self-serve interfaces for creating and improving tasks with quality checks inline.
   
   


YOU MAY BE A FIT IF

 - You’ve shipped full-stack products and owned systems from user interface through storage or services, using technologies such as TypeScript and React alongside Node, Python, or Go.

 - You’ve built dense, data-facing tools such as transcript viewers, diffing systems, review queues, observability products, or operational dashboards—and you have strong opinions about how structured data should be rendered.

 - You’ve built or maintained a design system or component library and can establish durable product and engineering conventions for a fast-moving team.

 - You’ve designed review, QA, moderation, fraud, or acceptance workflows where users had an incentive to get past the checks, and you know how to keep those systems honest.

 - You care about data quality, and are willing to inspect raw data. Experience with evaluations, graders, reinforcement learning, or data-quality systems is helpful but not required.

 - You move quickly under ambiguity, collaborate closely with researchers and domain experts, and take open-ended problems from rough need to reliable product.


APPLYING

If there appears to be a fit, we’ll schedule two or three short technical interviews focused on frontend craft for dense data and system design for a review-and-acceptance workflow. After that, we’ll invite you onsite to work on a small project using real rollouts, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Agent Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT OPENROUTER

OpenRouter is the leading AI routing and infrastructure layer that developers and enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize their AI use across models and providers. We help our customers avoid lock-in, capacity constraints, and unnecessary cost, giving them the flexibility to move fast, scale confidently, and stay future-proof as models evolve.

OpenRouter sits at the center of how developers discover, evaluate, integrate, and operate the world’s leading open and proprietary models.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring the first Product Manager for our Agent Platform, named Ori https://openrouter.ai/ori. Ori is our family of tools for putting any model to work in your terminal, in Slack, and on your desktop. Ori’s mission is to promote multi-model adoption at the application layer. Many agent tools today default to a single model family, locking teams in. Ori reflects our belief that the best agent experiences come from model diversity, built upon tools that enable seamless switching.

The Ori team moves fast: a small team built the current product in a few months. You’ll identify the strongest audience for each surface, decide where to focus, and set the goals for how we know it’s working. You’ll balance developers who live in the terminal and notice every detail with teams in Slack who want to teach their interns, agents that work alongside them, without it feeling like engineering. You’ll also ensure our tools are built upon primitives that enable the entire ecosystem to build multi-model apps.

You’ll work day-to-day with a small team led by one of our co-founders, alongside design, go-to-market, and the platform teams Ori is built on. This role is for a builder who has shipped developer tools end-to-end, uses coding agents daily, and wants to take a zero-to-one product from private testing to a business inside a company that already has distribution.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the agent platform roadmap end to end across Harness, Code, Eval, Intern, and Desktop, from the CLI today to teams of interns and multi-agent deployments.

 - Set the strategy. Define the target user and competitive positioning for each surface, and decide where Ori should invest across coding, cloud, and desktop agents. Position Ori as an open reference implementation to inspire the multi-model market.

 - Take new tools from waitlist to general availability. Run private testing and design partners, drive internal dogfooding, and instrument adoption, retention, and spend.

 - Make model fungibility real. Model switching, provider fallbacks, guaranteed tool dependencies, org guardrails, and eval-driven model selection that work in any harness and on any surface.

 - Own agent experience, from install and auth to CLI UX, harness configuration, secrets, connections, and the app interfaces. You’ll help us set the quality bar for new consumer-grade experiences.

 - Close the loop with go-to-market and the platform. Turn waitlist, tester, and enterprise signal into the roadmap, and push the API and SDK gaps Ori exposes into the core product.
   
   


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of product management or founder experience building developer tools, agent products, or infrastructure for technical users.

 - A zero-to-one track record. You have taken a product from prototype to paying users and are comfortable with the ambiguity and hard tradeoffs that come with it.

 - Daily fluency with coding agents. You use tools like Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, or OpenCode and have specific opinions about what makes an agent loop, a harness, or a tool integration good.

 - Strong technical judgment. You read code, run the CLI, inspect traces, and reason with engineers about agent loops, tool calling, context management, evals, and the cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs between models.

 - Strong product taste for developer tools. You’ve shipped technical products where interaction details matter, and can carry that judgment into new interfaces.

 - High agency and a bias toward action. You talk to users, prototype, ship, and iterate on a small team with fluid boundaries. You write clearly and often.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Founder or early employee of a developer tools or agent company.

 - Experience with multi-agent systems, agent skills or memory, or evals and benchmarking products.

 - Experience shipping Slack apps or native desktop apps, or growing a product with both developer and non-developer users.

 - Existing user of OpenRouter or active side projects in AI tooling.
   
   

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria above but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we’re looking for someone excited to join the team.
