jobs.description:
Company Overview

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

Kairos Power is seeking a highly motivated Systems Engineer to support the development and integration of advanced nuclear energy systems. In this role, you will apply disciplined systems engineering methods to translate program objectives, stakeholder needs, and design inputs into clear, verifiable technical requirements and integrated system solutions.

You will develop and maintain requirements, functional architectures, system architectures, interfaces, and verification strategies across multiple levels of the product and plant architecture. You will work closely with engineering disciplines, project management, licensing, quality, operations, suppliers, and external partners to identify integration concerns and resolve cross-functional technical issues.

The role will lead focused systems engineering activities, coordinate multidisciplinary technical reviews, evaluate the system-level impacts of proposed changes, and support the management of technical risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies throughout the engineering lifecycle. You will also mentor less-experienced engineers and contribute to the continuous improvement of Kairos Power systems engineering processes, tools, templates, training, and command media.

Responsibilities

• Develop, allocate, maintain, and trace technical requirements across multiple levels of product and plant architecture.

• Translate program objectives, stakeholder needs, design inputs, and regulatory considerations into clear, complete, consistent, and verifiable requirements.

• Perform and support functional analysis and decomposition to define required system behavior and establish traceability between functions, requirements, architecture, and verification activities.

• Develop and maintain functional, logical, and physical system architectures.

• Define, document, coordinate, and manage internal and external interfaces between systems, organizations, suppliers, facilities, and external partners.

• Develop verification strategies, methods, plans, acceptance criteria, and evidence needed to demonstrate that requirements have been satisfied.

• Coordinate and facilitate multidisciplinary requirements, architecture, interface, integration, and verification reviews.

• Maintain knowledge of and support compliance with applicable company procedures, codes, standards, and regulatory requirements.

• Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Relevant professional experience applying systems engineering methods to complex engineering programs or products.

• Experience developing, allocating, maintaining, and tracing technical requirements.

• Experience with one or more of the following: functional analysis and decomposition, system architecture development, interface definition and management, system integration, requirements verification and validation, technical change-impact assessment.

• Experience coordinating technical reviews or leading focused cross-functional engineering activities.

• Strong technical writing, communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

• Experience in the nuclear industry, power generation, aerospace, defense, energy, or another highly regulated industry is preferred.

• Experience using requirements management tools such as Jama Connect is preferred.

• Experience with model-based systems engineering methods and tools is preferred.

• Familiarity with applicable nuclear quality, licensing, safety, or regulatory practices is preferred.

• Experience supporting design reviews, trade studies, configuration management, or technical baseline management is preferred.

• Familiarity with relevant systems engineering standards and guidance, such as ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 or the INCOSE Systems Engineering Handbook is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

• Knowledge of systems engineering lifecycle processes and technical management practices.

• Knowledge of requirements development, decomposition, allocation, traceability, verification, and validation.

• Knowledge of functional, logical, and physical architecture development.

• Knowledge of interface identification, definition, documentation, and control.

• Knowledge of system integration, configuration management, and engineering change-control principles.

• Knowledge of technical risk, assumption, issue, opportunity, and dependency management.

• General knowledge of engineering design, licensing, quality, operations, and project execution within complex technical programs.

• Skill in writing clear, concise, implementation-independent, and verifiable technical requirements.

• Skill in performing functional analysis, architecture development, interface analysis, and change-impact assessment.

• Skill in using requirements management, modeling, analysis, and documentation tools.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, technical writing, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

• Ability to evaluate complex systems holistically and recognize interactions, dependencies, and unintended consequences.

• Ability to work collaboratively across engineering disciplines, organizations, and levels of technical authority.

• Ability to balance technical rigor with program cost, schedule, risk, and execution needs.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain attention to detail in a fast-paced engineering environment.

• Ability to proactively collect, organize, manage, and transfer technical knowledge.

Physical Demands

• Remaining in a stationary position, including sitting or standing, for prolonged periods.

• Moving about office, laboratory, manufacturing, or test-facility environments.

• Communicating with others to exchange technical information.

• Operating computers and other standard office equipment.

Environmental Conditions

• General office environment.

• High-concentration, demanding, and fast-paced work environment.

• Periodic work in prototyping, laboratory, test-facility, manufacturing, or industrial environments.

Safety and Personal Protective Equipment

• Reporting equipment issues, hazards, and unsafe conditions.

• Following applicable safety procedures and posted warning requirements.

• Wearing required personal protective equipment when entering laboratory, test, manufacturing, industrial, or controlled areas.

• Prioritizing the safety of oneself and others.

Travel

• Some travel may be required.

Additional Requirements

• Occasional schedule flexibility or extended hours may be required to support critical project milestones, technical reviews, testing, or integration activities.

jobs.title: Senior Regulatory Affairs Director - Oncology Cell & Gene Therapy
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Senior Director, Oncology Cell and Gene Therapy Regulatory Affairs, leads the development and implementation of the global regulatory strategy for CGT products of high complexity and visibility and may serve as Franchise GRL on complex programs with multiple indications. In addition to GRL responsibilities, the Sr RAD has the ability to function in dual capacity by also serving as a regional lead based on their location.

The Sr RAD ensures that the regulatory strategy is designed to deliver efficient approval with competitive labelling in keeping with the properties of the product(s) and the needs identified by the business, markets and patients. The Sr RAD provides team leadership and participates in coaching and mentorship to members of the relevant CGT Global Regulatory Strategy Team and is responsible for leading the global regulatory deliverables in line with GPT goals. The Sr RAD establishes external relationships with key Regulatory stakeholders, leveraging these to maintain competitive advantage. They are viewed as a Senior Leader within the Regulatory Community.

Typical Accountabilities

• Lead and own the development and implementation of the global regulatory strategy for a CGT product of high complexity, from current stage through BLA submission. May serve in dual-role as GRL and regional RAD.

• As a core member of the global product team, ensure that regulatory strategies are designed to deliver an efficient path to approval with competitive labeling in keeping with the properties of the product(s) and the needs identified by the business, markets and patients, and contribute to governance presentations.

• Lead regulatory strategy for all health authority meetings, responses to information requests, BLA development and submission, expedited pathway designations.

• Maintain a strong working knowledge of the relevant disease areas: early- and late-stage multiple myeloma.

• Lead a Global Regulatory Strategy Team (GRST) responsible for specific indications/programs within the franchise, key contributing members from the regions, emerging markets, RA CMC, Labeling and members of the submission and execution team. Participate in coaching and performance feedback to members of your GRST.

• Lead the objective assessment of emerging data against aspirations and update senior management on project risks/mitigation activities.

• Represent Regulatory Affairs on Global Product Teams (GPTs) providing strategic Regulatory advice and accountable for all Regulatory activities

• Accountable for the delivery of all project-related regulatory milestones, including assessment of the probability of regulatory success and mitigations. You will lead preparation of the regulatory strategy document and target product labeling.

• Demonstrate strategic, leadership, and collaboration skills, contributing to effective cross-functional teamwork in product development.

• Lead, participate, and promote non-project functional or cross-functional initiatives and engage externally on the corresponding topics as needed. Lead the development of novel regulatory tools and technology.

• Ensure appropriate planning and construction of the global dossier and core prescribing information led by the respective teams. Accountable for product maintenance and compliance activities associated with marketed brands.

• Partner with marketing companies (countries) and regional regulatory affairs staff to influence developing views/guidance.

• May have line management responsibilities in addition to matrixed supervisory, leadership, and mentoring roles.

Education, Qualifications, Skills and Experience

Essential

• An advanced degree in a science related field and seven-ten years of experience and/or appropriate knowledge/experience.

• Demonstrated success in cell and/or gene therapy regulatory strategy.

• Deep understanding of global regulatory science and integration with program strategy. Long standing experience of overall drug/biologic development processes and strategies for high profile, complex or novel development programs.

• Experience with product development for multiple myeloma.

• Broad background of experience working in pharmaceutical business and prior experience in several areas within regulatory affairs. Experience in Oncology (small molecules & biologics) is preferred.

• Proven experience leading regulatory and cross-functional teams, and stakeholder management.

• Ability to think strategically and critically and evaluate risks to regulatory activities.

• Previous experience in leading major Health Authority interactions.

• Excellent oral, written, and presentation skills.

• Strong organizational skills.

• Ability to work in a fast-paced environment in a hands-on fashion.

• Flexible and proactive, with the ability to manage multiple projects and successfully adapt to changing business needs and priorities.

Desirable

• Successful leadership of at least one global regulatory approval including leading response team and labeling negotiations

• Experience with FDA advisory committee and EMA oral explanation .

• Experience developing products for the treatment of autoimmune conditions.

• Experience working on due diligence activities and in a business alliance environment.

• Experience in leading and growing people through coaching or mentorship.

• Contribution to non-project business initiatives (e.g. at a portfolio or cross functional level)

At AstraZeneca, Regulatory professionals help turn breakthrough science into real solutions for patients with serious diseases by shaping innovative pathways through complex global requirements. Working with colleagues across locations, therapy areas and external partners, this role offers the chance to influence strategy end-to-end, from early development through rapid global approvals, while learning from leading experts, sharing best practices and using data, technology and modern approaches to reduce barriers for patients worldwide.

If this opportunity to drive transformative cell and gene therapies towards approval resonates, apply now to join us in bringing life-changing medicines to those who need them most.

jobs.title: Patient Journey Partner
jobs.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

At Roche, we believe better outcomes for more patients start with genuine partnership. As a Patient Journey Partner for Oncology, you will be a senior, empowered leader and the local face of Roche's healthcare ecosystem — partnering closely with everyone who touches the oncology patient journey to understand their needs and connect Roche's capabilities to co-create meaningful solutions. This is an integrated role spanning the full breadth of the patient journey, where your success is measured by the value you unlock for patients, their communities, and the healthcare system.

Your Opportunity

You will be directly accountable for delivering better outcomes for patients faster, with the decision-making authority to make an impact across the oncology patient journey in Indonesia.

• Act as a trusted partner and primary point of contact between healthcare stakeholders and Roche — bringing the outside in by uncovering opportunities to transform patient outcomes, and the inside out by connecting Roche's science and expertise to the ecosystem.
• Oversee the oncology patient journey end to end as a system thinker, identifying shared purpose among stakeholders and co-creating solutions that remove roadblocks for patients and the community.
• Own the customer engagement strategy for your area — from insight gathering through planning and implementation — in collaboration with fellow Patient Journey Partners, and capture timely stakeholder insights to drive data-informed action.
• Steward Roche's oncology portfolio through its lifecycle, supporting appropriate use and sharing the merits of our medicines with healthcare professionals in a truthful and balanced manner.
• Share patient and community needs internally, prioritize and secure resources, and pull in expertise from across the local affiliate and global network to deliver solutions faster.
• Ensure a consistently excellent experience whenever stakeholders engage with Roche's people, products, and services — and have the courage to stop activities that don't add predictable value for patients.

Who You Are

You bring personal purpose in improving the patient journey, a patient-centric and entrepreneurial mindset, and the integrity to lead as an open, honest, and genuine partner. You think at an enterprise level — beyond boundaries — to bring the best outcomes to Indonesia's health environment and across Roche globally.

• Deep understanding of the oncology patient journey and related treatments, enabling credible engagement with specialists, plus a robust grasp of medical affairs strategies and tactics including clinical research.
• In-depth understanding of the Indonesia healthcare system, its stakeholders, and the Indonesia Pharmaceutical Code of Conduct and related standards.
• Excellent stakeholder engagement and partnering skills — coaching, consulting, and deep listening — including partnership with therapeutic area experts; experience with patient advocacy groups is highly desired.
• Proven experience leading cross-functional teams; experience formulating cross-functional strategies is highly desired, along with strong business acumen spanning commercialization, medical, and customer experience.
• A growth mindset: you learn and unlearn quickly, experiment, take considered risks, make insight- and data-driven decisions, and share knowledge generously across networks.
• Comfortable understanding and using digital tools; experience in agile ways of working is desired.
• University degree in a scientific, economic, or business field; an advanced life science degree or MBA is a plus. Proficiency in English to collaborate across the broader Roche enterprise is highly desired.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Are you passionate about solving complex manufacturing challenges and driving continuous improvement? As a Focused Improvement Engineer, you will lead initiatives that improve safety, quality, productivity, cost, and equipment reliability across one of Unilever's flagship manufacturing operations. In this highly visible role, you will partner with cross-functional teams to eliminate losses, optimize packaging processes, implement new technologies, and deliver sustainable business results. If you thrive on data-driven problem solving and enjoy turning opportunities into measurable improvements, we'd love to hear from you.

Core Deliverables

Lead Continuous Improvement

• Own and execute the site's focused improvement agenda within the Packaging operation.
• Identify, prioritize, and eliminate manufacturing losses impacting safety, quality, waste, cost, and productivity.
• Lead projects that improve equipment performance, process capability, and operational efficiency.
• Deliver savings initiatives that strengthen the site's cost structure and business performance.

Optimize Manufacturing Processes

• Establish and maintain process standards, centerlines, and operating conditions that ensure consistent product quality and performance.
• Analyze production data to identify root causes of downtime, waste, defects, and process variation.
• Develop sustainable corrective actions to prevent recurrence and improve reliability.

Partner Across Functions

• Collaborate with Operations, Quality, R&D, Engineering, Safety, and external equipment suppliers to improve manufacturing capability.
• Support equipment upgrades, new technology implementation, process trials, and capital improvement projects.
• Serve as a key resource for World Class Manufacturing (WCM) and Unilever Manufacturing System (UMS) practices.

Develop Teams & Standards

• Create and maintain standard operating procedures, work instructions, and production standards.
• Train and coach operators on process control, loss elimination, and continuous improvement methodologies.
• Support Run-to-Standard activities and help build a culture of operational excellence.

Drive Digital & Future-Focused Solutions

• Co-lead DFOS implementation and become the site's subject matter expert for data collection and performance monitoring systems.
• Utilize manufacturing data and analytics to accelerate decision making and improve operational performance.

What Success Looks Like

• Improve line efficiency, reliability, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).
• Reduce waste, losses, quality defects, and operational costs.
• Deliver measurable productivity and savings improvements.
• Build sustainable standards that help teams consistently achieve performance targets.
• Influence a culture of continuous improvement across the manufacturing operation.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Industrial, Mechanical, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field.
• 3+ years of engineering, manufacturing, process, or packaging experience in a consumer products, food, personal care, chemical, or related manufacturing environment.
• Experience leading continuous improvement initiatives using TPM, WCM, Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies.
• Proven ability to analyze manufacturing data, identify root causes, and implement sustainable solutions.
• Experience leading end-to-end improvement projects focused on equipment performance, waste reduction, productivity, or quality improvement.
• Experience in a union manufacturing environment is a plus.
• Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt preferred.

Pay: The pay range for this position is $88,600 to $133,000. Unilever takes into consideration a wide range of factors that are utilized in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, qualifications and education, and other business and organizational needs.

Bonus: This position is bonus eligible.

Should the employee choose to participate, they can choose from a range of benefits to include, but is not limited to, health insurance (including prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage), retirement savings benefits, life insurance and disability benefits, parental leave, sick leave, paid vacation and holidays, as well as access to numerous voluntary benefits. Collins Aerospace, jednostka Raytheon Technologies Corporation (NYSE: RTX), jest liderem w zakresie zaawansowanych technologicznie i inteligentnych rozwiązań dla globalnego przemysłu lotniczego i obronnego. Stworzona w 2018 roku przez połączenie UTC Aerospace Systems i Rockwell Collins, Collins Aerospace ma możliwości, kompleksową ofertę i doświadczenie, aby sprostać najtrudniejszym wyzwaniom klientów i wymaganiom szybko rozwijającego się globalnego rynku. Nasze miejsce w strukturze korporacyjnej: UTC → Collins Aerospace → Mechanical Systems (SBU) → Landing Systems (BU).

Poza ustawowymi świadczeniami, RTX oferuje szeroki pakiet benefitów i nagród mających na celu wspieranie dobrego samopoczucia, rozwoju i sukcesów naszych pracowników.  Pracownicy mogą korzystać z programów takich jak program pomocy pracownikom, dofinansowanie do studiów, świadczenia emerytalne w ramach naszych planów emerytalnych, program motywacyjny oraz program uznania pracowników, który nagradza dobre wyniki.

Wynagrodzenie premiowe zależą od kilku czynników, w tym od wyników: indywidualnych, jednostki biznesowej oraz firmy. Zakres dostępnych benefitów może różnić się w zależności od poziomu stanowiska w strukturze organizacji oraz tego, czy stanowisko jest objęte układem zbiorowym pracy.

Job Summary:

The Military Engines Business Acquisition Center of Excellence (BACE) is establishing a new, strategic role that uniquely integrates proposal estimatingexpertise with proposal management leadership. As the first role of its kind, the Proposal Management and Estimating Lead will serve as a critical focal point for classified proposal efforts, leading both the development of robust cost estimates and the end‑to‑end proposal strategy, planning, and delivery process.

This P5 leader will independently drive proposal execution across complex, high‑visibility Military Engines programs, collaborating closely with the Business Acquisition Team (BAT), Program Management Office (PMO), Pricing, Contracts, and subject matter experts (SMEs) throughout the organization.

This role is onsite due to the classified nature of the work.

• Independently coordinate, lead, and develop comprehensive, compliant Basis of Estimates (BOEs) for all classified proposals.
• Manage proposal strategy, planning, schedules, and internal reviews.
• Validate, analyze, and challenge SME inputs and actuals to ensure accuracy, consistency, and defensible compliant estimating methodologies.
• Coordinate cross‑functional teams including the Business Acquisition Team (BAT), PMO, Pricing, Contracts, and SMEs.
• Lead responses to Requests for Information (RFIs) and fact‑finding; prepare negotiation support materials.
• Manage sweep Basis of Estimates (BOEs) and associated activities through contract award.

• Bachelor’s degree with 10+ years of relevant experience (project/program/proposal management, cost estimating, logistics, or related) OR an advanced degree and 7+ of years of relevant experience

• Experience leading complex proposals for military or government customers.
• Strong cost estimating background within aerospace/defense or a matrixed organization.

• Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to lead by influence and operate independently.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced, classified environment.

Job Description:

An opportunity for a Quality and Configuration Management Engineer has arisen within Airbus Defence and Space, Getafe (Madrid). The selected candidate will join the Quality & Product Assurance Team. The team is responsible for ensuring product conformity, regulatory compliance, and customer satisfaction across the entire aircraft life-cycle. Serving as the primary link between internal departments, civil/military authorities, and external customers, the team drives process improvements and maintains high quality standards.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Act as the main focal point within the Quality organization, safeguarding conformity and customer requirements while managing feedback to ensure continuous satisfaction.
• Manage relationships with Authorities (civil/military), ensuring organizational approvals (DOA, POA, MOA) are fulfilled, managing on-site quality assurance, and issuing flight permits.
• Support the Change Control Process and Configuration Baseline evolution, evaluating internal/external requirements and managing product breakdown structure changes.
• Ensure product delivery and lifecycle tracking ("As-built" vs design approved data) through assembly, functional/flight tests, customer delivery, and maintenance.
• Strengthen prevention and surveillance by defining and monitoring KPIs, analyzing non-conformances (NCRs), performing root cause analysis, and deploying recurrence prevention actions.
• Develop and maintain Quality Methods and instructions within the Quality Management System (QMS) while driving process efficiency improvements.

SKILLS

Is your profile aligned to the following list of skills? Apply! We are looking forward to know you:

• Education: Aeronautical Engineering, Industrial Engineering degree or a related discipline.
• Experience: Experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), or Configuration Management within the aerospace or defense industry.
• Soft skills: Proactive mindset, strong communication skills across cross-functional departments, customer-oriented attitude, and problem-solving capability.
• Languages: Advanced level in English. Spanish is highly valued.
• Technical knowledge: In-depth knowledge of aeronautical organizational approvals (DOA, POA, MOA), Quality Management Systems (QMS), Root Cause Analysis/NCR management, and Configuration Control processes.
• Valuable / Nice to have: Direct interaction experience with aviation authorities (EASA, PERAM, etc.) and flight permit processes.

Wells Fargo is seeking a visionary Principal Architect to lead the technology strategy and architectural direction of our enterprise collaboration ecosystem, one of the most critical technology domains powering productivity, communication, and innovation across the company. This is a rare opportunity to influence the future of workplace technology at scale, driving modernization efforts that impact every line of business and thousands of users across the organization.

As a trusted advisor to senior technology and business leaders, you will play a pivotal role in defining the target-state architecture for a complex portfolio of collaboration platforms and services. You'll partner with executives, product leaders, engineers, cybersecurity, risk, and enterprise architecture teams to guide strategic investments, accelerate transformation initiatives, strengthen resiliency, and shape the next generation of digital workplace experiences.

If you're energized by solving enterprise-scale challenges, influencing technology strategy, and leaving a lasting architectural footprint across a global organization, this role offers the visibility, scope, and impact to do exactly that.

From Microsoft 365 and enterprise messaging to AI-enabled productivity, unified communications, content collaboration, and workplace modernization, you'll help define what collaboration looks like for the future of Wells Fargo.

In this role, you will:

• Serve as a trusted advisor to senior and executive leadership—developing architectural frameworks and providing vision, direction, and domain expertise—for highly complex business and technical needs across multiple groups and the enterprise.

jobs.title: Strokovni sodelavec za oskrbo zdravil (m/ž/d) / Associate Expert Drug Supply (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Salary Range:

20.300,00 € - 37.700,00 €

Job Description Summary

Location: Menges, Slovenia #onsite

Role Purpose:
Z veseljem napovedujemo ustanovitev novega obrata klinične proizvodnje v Sloveniji, namenjenega hitrejšemu odkrivanju inovativnih zdravil za bolnike po vsem svetu. Najsodobnejši objekt, ki se nahaja v Biocampusu v Mengšu, nudi izjemno priložnost za sodelovanje na področju razvoja in proizvodnje inovativnih zdravil.

Iščemo navdušene in usposobljene strokovnjake za proizvodni tim. Kot strokovni sodelavec za oskrbo zdravil boste del tima Proizvodnih operacij.
Odgovorni boste za izvajanje proizvodnega procesa bioloških učinkovin, vključno s pripravo raztopin, upravljanjem bioreaktorjev, uporabo opreme za izolacijo učinkovine (kromatografski sistemi) in druga procesna oprema. Aktivnosti se izvajajo skladno z internimi postopki in zahtevami GxP.

Postanite del dinamičnega tima, ki na novo opredeljuje zdravljenje in prinaša upanje tistim, ki ga najbolj potrebujejo. Pridružite se nam pri oblikovanju prihodnosti varovanja zdravja in pri ustvarjanju pomembnih razlik v življenju bolnikov po vsem svetu. Veselimo se vašega prihoda v naš tim!
_____________

We are thrilled to announce the establishing of new clinical manufacturing facility in Slovenia, dedicated to accelerating the creation of innovative medicines for patients around the globe. This cutting-edge facility, located at Biocampus Mengeš, offers an exceptional opportunity for collaboration in the development and production of innovative medicines.

We are currently looking to hire passionate and skilled specialists in the Manufacturing Operations team.
As part of our team, you will be responsible for executing the production process of biological active substances, including the preparation of solutions, operation of bioreactors, use of equipment for active substance isolation such as chromatography systems, and other process equipment. Activities are performed in accordance with internal procedures and GxP requirements.

Be part of a dynamic team that is reimagining medicine and delivering hope to those who need it most. Join us in shaping the future of healthcare and making a meaningful difference in the lives of patients worldwide. We look forward to welcoming you to our team!

Job Description

Opis delovnega mesta

Vaše ključne odgovornosti:

• Izvedba procesa proizvodnje bioloških učinkovin, vključno z izvajanjem in-procesne analitike.
• Planiranje, izvajanje in dokumentiranje GxP aktivnosti.
• Izpolnjevanje GxP dokumentacije (dnevniki, obrazci, proizvodna poročila itd.), vključno s pregledom izvornih podatkov. Pisanje enostavnih postopkov, protokolov in poročil (delovni postopki, poročila o trendih itd.)
• Sodelovanje pri reševanju izzivov in odpravljanju težav. Prepoznavanje, sporočanje in prispevanje k reševanju odstopanj ter izvajanje korektivnih in preventivnih ukrepov. Uporaba pridobljenih izkušenj.
• Delovanje v skladu s standardi za kakovost, etiko, varnost, zdravje, okolje in informacijsko varnost ter zagotavljanje upoštevanja predpisov GxP.
• Odgovornost za osebni in strokovni razvoj.
• Izkazovanje pozitivne delovne etike in pozitivno vplivanje na druge.

Vaš doprinos k delovnem mestu:

• Srednješolska izobrazba.
• Tekoče znanje slovenščine. Tehnično znanje angleščine.
• Dobre organizacijske sposobnosti in sposobnosti upravljanja z dokumentacijo, ki zagotavljajo vodenje evidenc v skladu s pravili podjetja.
• Sposobnost natančnega upoštevanja navodil in postopkov.
• Ustrezno poznavanje programske opreme in računalniških orodij.

Zaželene izkušnje:

• Izkušenje s primerljivega delovnega mesta.
• Ustrezno strokovno ali tehnično znanje s področja naravoslovnih ved.
• Dobro poznavanje dobre proizvodne prakse (GMP) in izkušnje z delom v reguliranem proizvodnem okolju.

Z izbranim kandidatom bomo sklenili delovno razmerje za nedoločen čas s poskusno dobo 6 mesecev. Prijavo oddajte z življenjepisom v slovenskem jeziku.

Koristi in nagrade

V Novartisu smo zavezani skupnemu preoblikovanju medicine – in nagrajevanju ljudi, ki jo uresničijo.

Pričakovani letni osnovni plačni razpon za delovno mesto: €20,300 do €37,700

Osnovna plača je določena glede na spolno nevtralne cilje, kot so relevantne veščine, kompetence in izkušnje v skladu s politiko plač Novartisa, ob vstopu v Novartis pa se redno pregleduje.

Poleg osnovne plače ste morda upravičeni do bonusa na podlagi uspešnosti, odvisno od določenih parametrov uspešnosti.

Nagrade članstva v naši ekipi segajo daleč preko osnovne plače in spodbud. Ponujamo tudi različne konkurenčne ugodnosti, ki vam pomagajo uspevati osebno in poklicno, kot so zavarovalni načrti, pokojninski načrti, viri za dobrobit in globalni programi priznanja. Poleg tega ponujamo, kjer je mogoče, prilagodljive in hibridne možnosti dela ter najmanj 14 tednov plačanega starševskega dopusta.

Job description

Your key responsibilities:

• Executing the production process of biological active substances, including performing in-process analytics.
• Planning, performing, and documenting GxP activities.
• Completing GxP documentation, such as logs, forms, production reports, etc., including the review of source data. Writing simple procedures, protocols, and reports, such as work procedures, trend reports, etc.
• Participating in resolving challenges and troubleshooting. Identifying, reporting, and contributing to the resolution of deviations, as well as implementing corrective and preventive actions. Applying lessons learned.
• Acting in accordance with standards for quality, ethics, safety, health, environment, and information security, and ensuring compliance with GxP regulations.
• Taking responsibility for personal and professional development.
• Demonstrating a positive work ethic and positively influencing others.

Your contribution to the role:

• High school education.
• Fluent knowledge of Slovenian lenguage. Technical knowledge of English.
• Good organizational and documentation management skills, ensuring record-keeping in accordance with company rules.
• Ability to follow instructions and procedures accurately.
• Appropriate knowledge of software and computer tools.

Desired experience:

• Experience in a comparable role.
• Relevant professional or technical knowledge in the field of natural sciences.
• Good knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practice, GMP, and experience working in a regulated manufacturing environment.

An employment contract will be concluded with the selected candidate for a permanent contract, with a 6-month probationary period. Please submit your application with a CV in Slovenian language.

Benefits & Rewards

At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen.

Expected Annual Base Salary Range for role: €20,300 to €37,700

The base salary offered is determined based on gender-neutral objectives, such as relevant skills, competencies and experience in accordance with the Novartis pay setting policy and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically.

In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus depending on certain performance parameters.

The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives. We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. In addition, we provide flexible and hybrid working options, where possible, and minimum 14 weeks paid parental leave.

jobs.title: Logistics & Distribution Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

General Summary:

The Manager, Temperature Controlled Logistics (TCL) is responsible for supporting the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of processes and procedures that enable reliable, compliant temperature-controlled logistics operations across Vertex. This role partners closely with Logistics Operations teams across all modalities, Logistics Service Providers, Quality Assurance, Packaging Engineering, Supply Chain, Technical Operations, Trade Compliance, Sourcing & Procurement, and internal and external manufacturing organizations to ensure product quality, regulatory compliance, and evolving business needs are consistently met.

The successful candidate will help design, build, and sustain a robust logistics network that supports pipeline and commercial programs. Key responsibilities include evaluating and deploying innovative active and passive packaging solutions; assessing IoT-enabled monitoring devices and temperature data loggers; and evaluating vendor systems and data capabilities to enable real-time monitoring of shipment integrity and temperature conditions. The Manager will also oversee logistics quality-system activities, including change controls, from initiation through closure.

This position requires a collaborative, data-driven leader with a strong quality and compliance mindset, deep cold-chain logistics expertise, and the ability to anticipate, troubleshoot, and resolve complex operational issues in a fast-paced environment.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:

• Develop, implement, and maintain standard operating procedures, work instructions, and packaging instructions that enable compliant logistics activities across the Global Supply Chain and Internal and External manufacturing network, in alignment with Logistics Service Providers.
• Ensure temperature-controlled logistics processes consistently support product quality, regulatory requirements, and business objectives. Serve as the primary point of contact for shipping and validation activities during Health Authority inspections and internal audits.
• Manage logistics related quality system activities, including deviations, corrective and preventive actions, after-action reviews, and associated remediation activities.
• Own the development and maintenance of Logistics Validation Master Plans supporting the validation of shipping and storage activities across modalities and product types throughout the product lifecycle, from clinical development through commercial operations.
• Partner with Product and Program Teams to support product launches, lifecycle-management activities, and evolving temperature-controlled logistics requirements.
• Support supplier qualification, transportation lane selection, risk assessments, and transportation mode decisions for temperature-controlled shipments, including the selection of qualified active and passive packaging solutions.
• Own the periodic review and maintenance of the internal Logistics Risk Assessment tool, including lane and route data, in close partnership with Logistics Operations teams and Logistics Service Providers.
• Collaborate with Logistics Operations, DTE, Quality, and other cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate, implement, launch, and continuously enhance logistics and supply chain information systems.
• Define, measure, analyze, and communicate temperature-controlled logistics key performance indicators and supporting metrics to assess logistics and distribution performance and identify improvement opportunities.
• Participate in quality exception investigations and lead the resolution of complex cold-chain and logistics issues, including implementation of remediation and preventive measures.
• Lead process redesign workshops, manage process changes, and identify opportunities to improve operational performance, compliance, and scalability.
• Facilitate cross-functional process workshops to gather requirements, align stakeholders, and translate business needs into sustainable, scalable process improvements.
• Champion change management activities by educating stakeholders and supporting business users responsible for operating logistics processes, newly implemented capabilities, and temperature-controlled solutions.
• Establish work plans and prioritize activities for external workforce resources and third party companies supporting shipping validation studies. Ensure work is delivered in accordance with internal policies and procedures, required timelines, and approved budgets.
• Support the development and coordination of statements of work for applicable subcontracted services and monitor invoices for related activities.

Knowledge and Skills:

• Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline
• 5-7+ years progressive experience in Engineering, Quality and/or Manufacturing roles in the pharmaceutical industry – Experience with Clinical/Commercial drug, device and/or combination products across Biologics and Genetic and Cell Therapy technologies.
• Master’s degree in business or supply chain or industrial engineering or finance preferred.
• Experience in leading development and implementation of packaging solutions used in logistics activities across complex logistics operations.
• Thought leader in Logistics, Warehousing and Transportation with a proven ability to innovate and implement practical, compliant solutions.
• Proven ability to work seamlessly across teams and develop excellent partnerships with peers.
• Demonstrated experience of the principles and regulations associated with GDP / GxP compliance.

Education and Experience:

• Direct experience managing temperature-controlled and cold-chain logistics for small-molecule, cell therapy, and gene therapy programs, including short-lead-time operations.
• Experience managing logistics across internal manufacturing sites, external manufacturing partners, and CDMOs.
• Strong knowledge of Good Distribution Practices, trade-compliance requirements, and regulations related to hazardous shipments, employee safety, and freight classifications.
• Working knowledge of logistics technology and data integrations, including Transportation Management Systems, Warehouse Management Systems, and carrier integrations.
• Strong analytical and data-driven approach to evaluating performance, identifying risks, and developing practical solutions.
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including tables, arrays, formulas, and conditional formatting.
• Demonstrated ability to anticipate operational risks, develop effective contingency plans, and resolve complex logistics issues through critical thinking and creative problem-solving.
• Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex issues and solutions effectively across the organization.
• Proven ability to build trusted relationships, influence stakeholders, and create alignment across cross-functional teams and all organizational levels.
• Strong organizational, time-management, and prioritization skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively in a collaborative, fast-paced, and evolving environment.
• Sound business judgment, flexibility, and the ability to manage change while maintaining focus on quality, compliance, and operational performance.
• Demonstrated supervisory and resource-management capabilities, including the ability to develop team members and optimize budgets, staffing, technology, and other resources to achieve business objectives.
• Professional certifications and membership in Professional Associations (APICS CLTD, CSCP) is strongly preferred.

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.

Pay Range:

$111,800 - $167,600

Disclosure Statement:

The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations.  From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more.

Flex Designation:

Remote-Eligible

Flex Eligibility Status:

In this Remote-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as:
1.    Remote: work remotely five days per week and come into the office on occasion – you’re always welcome on-site; or select
2.    Hybrid: work remotely up to two days per week; or select
3.    On-Site: work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility.

Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time.

As an AI Engineer specializing in Agentic AI, you will develop intelligent agents that can autonomously perceive, reason, and act in dynamic environments as part of Zoom AI Companion (AIC).

Your work will directly impact the Zoom user experience by designing and implementing innovative algorithms and systems. We are part of the Zoom AI Vertical Organization, dedicated to enhancing the Zoom user experience in workplace and customer interactions. Our team of innovative thinkers is focused on creating the next generation of AI technologies that can autonomously understand, learn, and adapt to improve user engagement and satisfaction. • Designing and implementing backend orchestration layers between AI components within microservices, focusing on agent workflows and runtime operations.
• Building scalable LLM-powered systems including RAG pipelines, tool-use workflows, and multi-step reasoning agents.

jobs.description:
Why Wells Fargo:

Are you looking for more? Find it here. At Wells Fargo, we're more than a financial services leader – we’re a global trailblazer committed to driving innovation, empowering communities, and helping our customers succeed. We believe that a meaningful career is much more than just a job – it’s about finding all of the elements to help you thrive, in one place. Living the Well Life means you’re supported in life, not just work. It means having robust benefits, competitive compensation, and programs designed to help you find work-life balance and well-being. You’ll be rewarded for investing in your community, celebrated for being your authentic self, and empowered to grow. And we’re recognized for it – Wells Fargo once again ranked in the top five on the 2026 LinkedIn Top Companies list of best workplaces “to grow your career” in the U.S. Join us!

About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Teller to join our National Branch Network. In this front line, customer focused role, you will support customers’ everyday banking needs through in-branch interactions, completing transactions accurately while delivering a welcoming and reliable experience. As a primary point of contact for customers, you represent the branch through strong service, attention to detail, and genuine care.

As a Teller, you will build foundational banking skills while learning about customers’ needs and introducing them to helpful products, services, and digital tools. You will identify opportunities to support customers and connect them to the right banker for more detailed product conversations. You will work closely with branch teammates to keep daily operations running smoothly and deliver a consistent, high-quality customer experience. This role offers meaningful exposure to retail banking and serves as an excellent starting point for long-term growth and career mobility, supported by Wells Fargo’s training, coaching, and team-based culture.

jobs.title: Head of Sales - Getnet Platforms
jobs.description:
Head of Sales - Getnet Platforms

Country: Spain

ABOUT GETNET PLATFORMS

Getnet Platforms is part of Santander Payment Solutions and brings together a portfolio of strategic software platforms powering Santander’s global payments ecosystem.

Our cloud-native SaaS solutions cover critical payment capabilities across the value chain, including account-to-account processing, card issuing and processing, FX services, SWIFT connectivity, fraud management, payment orchestration, and other payment infrastructure services.

Having been built and proven at scale within Santander, our platforms are now entering a new phase of growth: expanding into the open market and enabling banks, PSPs, fintechs and regulated financial institutions worldwide to accelerate their payment capabilities through modern, scalable technology.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are seeking a commercially driven and entrepreneurial Head of Sales to lead the expansion of Getnet Platforms into the open market.

This role will be responsible for defining and executing the go-to-market strategy, building a scalable sales organization, developing strategic partnerships, and driving revenue growth across Europe, LATAM and America.

The successful candidate will combine deep expertise in payments and financial technology with a proven track record of selling complex SaaS and platform solutions to enterprise clients.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Commercial Strategy & Growth

• Define and execute the commercial strategy for Getnet Platforms’ SaaS and payment infrastructure solutions.
• Build and scale the open-market sales motion.
• Develop and manage the sales pipeline, ensuring sustainable growth and achievement of revenue targets.
• Identify new market opportunities, customer segments, and strategic partnerships to accelerate expansion.
• Drive customer acquisition, retention, and long-term account growth.

Enterprise Sales Leadership

• Lead complex enterprise sales cycles from prospecting through contract negotiation and closing.
• Understanding of decision-making hierarchies in key financial services industry, combined with the ability to connect with key counterparts where relationships become an entry need to sales
• Build executive-level relationships with banks, PSPs, fintechs, embedded finance providers, and regulated financial institutions.
• Develop value propositions tailored to different customer segments and market needs.
• Create scalable sales methodologies, processes, and performance frameworks.

Ecosystem & Partnerships

• Establish strategic alliances with technology providers, payment networks, consulting firms, and industry partners.
• Represent Getnet Platforms at industry events, conferences, and executive forums.
• Position Getnet Platforms as a leading provider of payment technology infrastructure.

Leadership

• Build, coach, and lead a high-performing international sales organization.
• Collaborate closely with Product, Technology, Marketing, Strategy, and Operations teams.
• Foster a culture of accountability, customer focus, and commercial excellence.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Experience

• 12+ years of experience in senior commercial leadership roles within payments, fintech, banking technology, SaaS, or platform businesses.
• Proven experience building and scaling new revenue streams, business units, or open-market commercial organizations.
• Demonstrated success selling complex B2B SaaS, platform, infrastructure, or mission-critical technology solutions.
• Strong track record of exceeding revenue targets and managing multi-million-euro sales pipelines.
• Experience operating across multiple European markets and international environments.

Industry Expertise

• Deep understanding of the payment’s ecosystem, including account-to-account payments, card issuing and processing, payment acceptance, payment orchestration, and related infrastructure.
• Knowledge of payment schemes, regulatory frameworks, and emerging payment technologies.
• Experience working with banks, PSPs, fintechs, embedded finance providers, or regulated financial institutions.

Leadership Capabilities

• Ability to understand evolving product capabilities and match them autonomously against leads and opportunities, committing on needs not yet ready but feasible and declining on needs where delivery would be unlikely.
• Ability to understand the big picture of a financial services institution needs on payments (core systems, onboarding, risk, channels, fraud) in relation to the elements that will be part of the sales portfolio.
• Entrepreneurial mindset with a strong ability to create and scale new business opportunities.
• Exceptional negotiation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to operate effectively in complex matrix organizations.
• Strong people leadership and team development capabilities.

Education & Languages

• Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance, Technology, Engineering, or related field.
• MBA or equivalent postgraduate qualification preferred.
• Fluent Spanish and English required.
• Portuguese highly valued.

SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE WILL BE MEASURED BY

• Revenue growth from open-market clients.
• New customer acquisition.
• Strategic partnership development.
• Sales pipeline quality and conversion rates.
• Geographic expansion and market penetration.
• Team performance and organizational capability building.

Join us in shaping the future of payments technology and building the next generation of SaaS platforms powering financial institutions worldwide.

As part of Kellanova’s Away from Home (AFH) team, you’ll support financial strategy for products sold outside traditional grocery channels—think convenience stores, cafeterias, college campuses, and airports. You’ll play a key role in budgeting and forecasting, managing monthly close processes, and building full P&Ls that feed into Kellanova North America (KNA) Finance. This is a hands-on role requiring strong analytical skills and advanced Excel proficiency to drive insights and support decision-making.

What are we looking for?

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance or related field
• Strong experience in budgeting, forecasting, and full P&L ownership
• Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs)
• Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines
• Strong analytical skills with a knack for storytelling through data
• Excellent communication skills and comfort working across teams

What will your key responsibilities be?

• Budgeting, Forecasting & Reporting – Lead monthly forecasting cycles and support annual budget development. Own the monthly close process for the Away from Home business and build complete P&Ls that roll up to KNA Finance. Perform ROI and variance analysis to support business decisions.
• Analytical Storytelling – Break down financial data to uncover trends and drivers. Respond to ad hoc requests with clear, actionable insights that help tell the story behind the numbers.
• Process Ownership – Work independently to manage reporting requirements and improve efficiency in budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis. Excel will be your primary tool—think pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, and offline modeling.
• Cross-Functional Collaboration – Partner with Sales Finance, Commercial Strategy, Supply Chain, and Marketing to gather inputs and drive performance. Exposure to the AFH CFO and KNA Finance teams is part of the role.

What can you expect from Mars?

• Work with over 170,000 diverse and talented Associates, all guided by The Five Principles.
• Join a purpose driven company, where we are striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
• Best-in-class learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
• An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

jobs.title: Associate Specialist (Cell Therapy Manufacturing)
jobs.description:
Associate Specialist (Cell Therapy Manufacturing)

Introduction to role

Are you ready to bring precision and initiative to the start-up of a new cell therapy manufacturing facility—seeing your work translate into clinical trials that could change patients’ lives? Join a team producing next-generation cell therapy products at a pivotal moment as our first clinical batches move from process development into cGMP operation.

In this visible, hands-on role, you will collaborate daily with Process Development, Clinical Operations, Materials Management, and Quality to turn robust science into reliable manufacturing outcomes. You will help build the documentation, run sophisticated automated equipment in Grades A and B cleanrooms, and lead by example on the floor to keep every batch on track. Can you picture yourself owning a “right first time” mindset and guiding a shift handover that keeps a critical lot moving?

Accountabilities

• GMP Documentation Excellence: Author and execute manufacturing batch records, work instructions, and SOPs with a “right first time” mindset; maintain bills of materials; reconcile batches promptly; document all activities to meet cGMP requirements; assist with deviations, non-conformances, and OOS investigations. Your rigor reduces errors, speeds release, and strengthens audit readiness.
• Aseptic Equipment Operations: Monitor, clean, prepare, and operate automated cell processing, cell expansion, and filling equipment in Grades A and B cleanrooms. Your care and consistency protect product quality and patient safety.
• Training and Knowledge Transfer: Train personnel on aseptic processing, equipment operation, cGMPs, documentation, and technical theory. By elevating team capability, you increase throughput and reliability.
• Document Review and Continuous Improvement: Review batch records, SOPs, and logbooks for completeness, clarity, and accuracy; submit edits for revision as needed. Your attention to detail drives procedural clarity and repeatability.
• Tech Transfer and Process Development: Participate in tech transfer activities; support development of platform processes; contribute to study and experiment designs; modify or improve processes and systems when appropriate. Your input helps mature processes from concept to cGMP readiness.
• Floor Leadership and Problem Solving: Provide technical instruction; allocate administrative tasks; assign work to manufacturing staff; lead activities on the manufacturing floor; communicate product status at shift change; troubleshoot processing and equipment issues. Your leadership keeps operations aligned, responsive, and efficient.
• Safety and Compliance Stewardship: Ensure a safe work environment in accordance with AstraZeneca standards. Your vigilance fosters a strong safety culture.
• Flexibility: Weekend work may be required. Your adaptability ensures continuity of critical manufacturing runs.

Essential Skills/Experience

• Bachelor’s degree with 0-3 years of general cGMP manufacturing experience or a Master’s degree in life sciences, engineering, or a related field with 0-2 years of general cGMP manufacturing experience
• Basic knowledge in biologics manufacturing process, cell culture and/or vector products.
• Technical proficiency in aseptic technique and working with manufacturing equipment in open and closed systems.
• Working knowledge of automated manufacturing equipment and/or process analytical technologies.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and data analysis.

Desirable Skills/Experience

• Previous manufacturing or process development experience with cell therapy or vector products.
• Dynamic individual with the ability to communicate and engage others.
• Independent and self-starting. Ability to work with minimal supervision.
• Demonstrate flexibility and willingness to change ways of working/identify opportunities to improve processes within cGMP clinical manufacturing environment.

Why AstraZeneca

Here, your work sits close to the decision point and the patient impact. You will operate at the forefront of science with high visibility, shaping end deliverables across therapy areas and collaborating with unexpected teams in the same room to unleash bold thinking. We balance ambition with support—leaders empower you to improve, experiments are celebrated for what they teach, and resilient minds find inventive paths through a heavily regulated environment. You will expand your skills as you apply advanced technologies to complex problems, contribute to enterprise-recognized work, and bring courage and curiosity to challenges that truly matter. We value kindness alongside ambition, and we back people who speak up, share opinions, and turn critique into better solutions.

Step into this high-exposure manufacturing role and help deliver transformative cell therapies to patients—take the next step today and show us how your precision and initiative will raise our standards!

The annual base pay for this position ranges from $65,082 to $97,622. Our positions offer eligibility for various incentives—an opportunity to receive short-term incentive bonuses, equity-based awards for salaried roles and commissions for sales roles. Benefits offered include qualified retirement programs, paid time off (i.e., vacation, holiday, and leaves), as well as health, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.

jobs.title: Director, Agent Intelligence
jobs.description:
Job Description

We are seeking an experienced AI engineering leader to build and operate Vertex's Agent Intelligence layer: the memory, personas, skills, and flagship agent experiences that make every Vertex AI agent grounded, consistent, and effective. Vertex Pharmaceuticals is in a transformational period, and the AI team is at the center of our AI-first strategy, delivering solutions that empower executives, researchers, and business users to make faster, more confident decisions.

As part of the Vertex Data team, you will lead the Agent Intelligence function within Knowledge & Grounding. You will own the four primitives that all Vertex agents are built from: agent memory (personal and organizational), personas as code, skills (atomic tools and higher-order compositions), and the flagship agents that put those primitives to work on Vertex's hardest use cases.

As the Director of Agent Intelligence, you will build the reusable building blocks of agent intelligence at Vertex. Your work will multiply the velocity and quality of agent development across Vertex, ensuring every agent benefits from a common foundation of grounded, governed, and reusable intelligence.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:

• Agent Memory. Design and operate Vertex's agent memory layer, spanning personal memory (per-user, per-session continuity) and organizational memory (shared institutional knowledge agents accumulate and reuse), including retention, retrieval, conflict resolution, and classification policies.
• Personas as Code. Define and steward the persona system that gives Vertex agents their voice, remit, and boundaries, including versioning, review, composition, and deployment workflows.
• Skills Catalog & Compositions. Curate the catalog of atomic tools agents can call (retrieval, analytics, action) and the higher-order skill compositions that combine them into persona-specific workflows, with clear contracts, registry, and quality standards.
• Flagship Agent Development. Design, build, and deploy custom AI agents for Vertex's highest-value enterprise use cases using Snowflake Cortex AI, Databricks AI, and agent orchestration frameworks, using these builds to harden the underlying primitives.
• Enterprise Agent Standards. Define and maintain the enterprise standards for agent orchestration, prompt libraries, persona definitions, tool-use patterns, and response quality that all teams must follow, regardless of builder.
• Experience Consistency & UX Standards. Define the quality bar for conversational UX across the enterprise (tone/persona, citation patterns, error handling, escalation paths, transparency) and drive consistency across agents.
• Prompt & Skill Library Stewardship. Curate and govern reusable prompt and skill assets (system prompts, persona templates, tool instructions, conversation patterns) with documentation and contribution workflows.

Knowledge and Skills:

• AI Agent Expertise. Hands-on experience building production AI agents using frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or similar orchestration tools.
• Cloud AI Platforms. Strong experience with Snowflake (Cortex AI, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search) and/or Databricks (Agent Bricks, AI Functions, Mosaic AI) in enterprise environments.
• Full-Stack AI Engineering. Ability to work across the full AI stack, including data preparation, prompt engineering, agent orchestration, evaluation/testing, deployment, and monitoring.
• Memory & State Design. Direct experience designing how agents remember, including session state, long-horizon memory, retrieval over conversational history, and the data model behind it.
• Production Operations. Track record of operating AI systems in production with high availability, monitoring, and continuous improvement.
• Leadership & Communication. Proven ability to lead technical teams, communicate with executive stakeholders, and translate business needs into AI solutions.
• Pharma or Life Sciences Context. Experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, or life sciences data environments. Familiarity with clinical, regulatory, and commercial data domains is a plus.
• Platform Primitive Design. Experience designing reusable agent abstractions such as persona frameworks, skill registries, or tool catalogs.
• Agent Evaluation Tooling. Familiarity with evaluation tooling such as Braintrust, LangSmith, Mosaic AI Agent Evaluation, Arize, or Ragas.
• Model Customization. Experience with model fine-tuning, distillation, or post-training for domain adaptation.

Education and Experience:

• 10+ years of experience in data engineering, AI/ML, or advanced analytics, with 3+ years specifically focused on NLP systems, AI agent development, or conversational AI.

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.

Pay Range:

$216,400 - $324,600

Disclosure Statement:

The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations.  From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more.

Flex Designation:

Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible

Flex Eligibility Status:

In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as:
1.    Hybrid: work remotely up to two days per week; or select
2.    On-Site: work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility.

Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time.

Behavioral Health Technician (Full-Time)

Saint Mary’s Behavioral Health Center (SMBHC)

Saint Mary’s Behavioral Health Center is an evidence-based, client-centered residential treatment program dedicated to meeting clients where they are and helping them “be the great person they were always meant to be.” We provide a warm, welcoming, and therapeutic environment for adolescents receiving mental health treatment.

We are currently seeking Behavioral Health Technicians to provide safe monitoring, support, and structure for clients in our primary mental health residential program.

Schedule

• 1st Shift: 7:00 AM – 3:30 PM
• 2nd Shift: 3:00 PM – 11:30 PM

• 3rd Shift: 11:00 PM - 7:30 AM

Pay

• Starting at $17.00/hour

Employment Type

• Full-Time & Part -Time

Position Overview

The Behavioral Health Technician (BHT) is a vital member of the treatment team and works under the supervision of the Director of Housing and Transportation. This role is responsible for ensuring the safety, care, and well-being of clients, maintaining a supportive therapeutic environment, and accurately documenting client behavior.

This position is ideal for individuals who:

• Can problem-solve effectively
• Make sound decisions during crisis situations
• Are interested in growing and advancing in the mental health field
• Thrive in a dynamic, challenging, and rewarding environment

Population Served

• Adolescents ages 11–17 (up to age 19)
• Clients receiving residential treatment for:Self-harmAggressionSuicidal ideationSubstance abuseTraumaMood instabilityDepression and anxiety

Knowledge & Training Requirements

• Ability to interact professionally with clients and staff
• Ability to handle stressful and demanding situations
• Strong collaboration skills within a multidisciplinary treatment team
• Competency in problem-solving, stress management, ethics, and teamwork
• Knowledge of alcohol and other drugs, including their physical, emotional, intellectual, and spiritual impact
• Ability to recognize medical emergencies and take appropriate action
• Knowledge of emergency procedures, First Aid, and CPR
• Flexibility to adapt to schedule changes and additional responsibilities related to mental health treatment

Key Responsibilities

• Maintain a safe, therapeutic environment for clients and staff
• Monitor, observe, and document client behavior and accountability
• Supervise self-administered medications
• Complete and submit incident reports promptly
• Attend all staff meetings and mandatory in-services
• Follow infection control guidelines at all times
• Provide end-of-shift reports to the Director via email
• Report medical emergencies, elopements, or ACA incidents immediately
• Transport clients to appointments, activities, support groups, and other facilities using a company van
• Orient new clients and complete housing intake documentation
• Conduct searches of client belongings and residential spaces for contraband
• Monitor curfews and rule compliance for transitional living clients

Qualifications

• High School Diploma or equivalent
• CPR Certification preferred (training provided if needed)
• 0–1 years of experience preferred (not required) in:Mental healthChemical dependencyPsychiatric, residential, partial hospitalization, or outpatient settings

Benefits

• Paid Time Off (PTO)
• Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
• Life Insurance
• Paid Holidays
• Opportunities for Advancement
• Free CPI Training
• Free CPR Training

This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way.

We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences.
